n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.anchor.zh: 「正因为……所以更……」——原因越强，结果越被放大。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.anchor.en: “Precisely because…” — the stronger the cause, the more it amplifies the result.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.logic.zh: A 的程度、经历或期待很高，于是 B 的感受也被推高。好坏都行：期待していただけに残念だ，努力しただけに嬉しい。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.logic.en: A is strong in degree, experience or expectation, so the feeling in B is raised accordingly. It works both ways: 期待していただけに残念だ and 努力しただけに嬉しい.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.connection.zh: 动词・い形容词普通形／な形容词词干＋な／名词＋だけに
n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.connection.en: Verb or i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な / noun + だけに

n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.contrast.zh: 「だけあって」偏正面评价，“不愧是”；「だけに」只讲因果被放大，好坏都行。别只凭正负面色硬分——「経験が長いだけに説明が上手だ」也完全成立。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.contrast.en: だけあって leans positive, as in no wonder; だけに only says the cause is amplified and works either way. Do not split them by positive versus negative alone — 経験が長いだけに説明が上手だ is perfectly fine.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.translation.zh: 正因为之前特别期待，失败时才格外失望。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.2.translation.en: I had expected so much that the failure hurt all the more.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.anchor.zh: 「不愧是……」——看到结果，感叹果然和身份相称。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.anchor.en: “Just like you'd expect from…” — the result matches the reputation.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.logic.zh: 先看到符合身份、经验或评价的结果，再回头感叹“难怪”。几乎都用于积极评价，常和「さすが」一起出现。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.logic.en: The result fits the status, experience or reputation, and the speaker looks back and says no wonder. It is almost always positive and often appears with さすが.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词・い形容词普通形／な形容词词干＋な／名词＋だけあって
n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.connection.en: Verb or i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な / noun + だけあって

n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.contrast.zh: 和「だけに」有重叠，区别在重心：だけあって落在“评价果然没错”，だけに落在“原因强所以结果强”。负面结果用だけあって会不自然。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.contrast.en: It overlaps with だけに but the weight differs: だけあって lands on the reputation being deserved, だけに on the cause being strong. With a bad result, だけあって sounds odd.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.translation.zh: 不愧是学了十年日语，发音就是很自然。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.3.translation.en: Ten years of studying Japanese show — his pronunciation is remarkably natural.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.anchor.zh: 「不枉……」——回头给先前的付出结账：这份投入值。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.anchor.en: “Worth every bit of…” — settles the bill on earlier effort and finds it paid off.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.logic.zh: 看到成果之后，评价之前的努力、花费、等待或名声确实没有白费。句尾固定，前面多用た形，带满足感。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.logic.en: After seeing the result, the speaker judges that the effort, expense, wait or reputation was not wasted. The ending is fixed, usually after a た-form, and carries satisfaction.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.connection.zh: 普通形＋だけのことはある（常见：た形＋だけのことはある）
n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.connection.en: Plain form + だけのことはある (usually た-form + だけのことはある)

n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.contrast.zh: 「だけあって」说“身份与结果相称”，「だけのことはある」说“付出没白费”。排队两小时吃拉面，用后者；说名校毕业果然厉害，用前者。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.contrast.en: だけあって says status matches result; だけのことはある says the outlay was worth it. For queueing two hours for ramen, use the latter; for a famous school living up to its name, the former.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.translation.zh: 不枉排了两个小时队，这碗拉面确实好吃。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.4.translation.en: Two hours in the queue was worth it — this ramen is genuinely good.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.anchor.zh: 「光是……就……」——只这一个条件，结果就已经发生。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.anchor.en: “Just … is enough to…” — one condition alone already produces the result.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.logic.zh: 满足 A 这一项，B 就成立，带“甚至不需要更多”的感觉。常和「思い出す」「分かる」「泣ける」这类反应动词搭配。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.logic.en: Satisfying A alone is enough for B, with the sense that nothing more is needed. It often pairs with reactions such as 思い出す, 分かる or 泣ける.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.contrast.zh: 别机械译成“只有”。后项已经成立时，中文自然是“光是 A 就 B”；译成“只有”会让句子读不通。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.contrast.en: Do not render it mechanically as 只有. When the second half has already happened, Chinese wants 光是 A 就 B, and 只有 makes the sentence unreadable.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.translation.zh: 光是看到这张照片，就会想起那次旅行。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.5.translation.en: Just looking at this photo brings the trip back.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.anchor.zh: 「光靠……还不够」——A 单独撑不起后项。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.anchor.en: “A alone is not enough” — one condition cannot carry the result.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.logic.zh: 后面几乎都是否定判断：「足りない」「できない」「難しい」「無理だ」。用来指出还缺别的条件，语气是提醒而不是责备。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.logic.en: The second half is nearly always negative: 足りない, できない, 難しい, 無理だ. It points out that something else is still missing, as a reminder rather than a rebuke.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.connection.en: Noun / plain form + だけでは

n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.contrast.zh: 「だけで」说 A 已经够，带来了 B；「だけでは」正相反，说 A 还不够。一个肯定一个否定，看到句尾的「ない」就知道是后者。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.contrast.en: だけで says A is already enough and B follows; だけでは says the opposite, that A is not enough. One affirms, one denies, and a ない at the end tells you it is the second.

n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.translation.zh: 光靠读教科书，还练不出自然的会话。
n2.day4-dake.grammar.6.translation.en: Reading the textbook alone will not give you natural conversation.

n2.day4-dake.question.0.explanation.zh: 「調べられるだけ調べる」表示在能力和时间允许的范围内尽可能多查，不是只查一点。
n2.day4-dake.question.0.explanation.en: The " 調べられるだけ調べる " indicates that as many searches as possible, not just a few, are possible within the limits of capacity and time.

n2.day4-dake.question.0.anchor.en: It's as much as it takes.

n2.day4-dake.question.1.explanation.zh: 这里要求在可能范围内早点到，用「できるだけ」自然对应“尽量”。
n2.day4-dake.question.1.explanation.en: Here's the requirement to arrive as early as possible, using "できるだけ" for "as much as possible".

n2.day4-dake.question.2.explanation.zh: 「だけに」偏重原因使结果更强烈；「だけあって」偏重结果与经历或投入相称。本句中两种表达均可自然成立，不用结果的好坏机械区分，因此两项都计分。
n2.day4-dake.question.2.explanation.en: だけに emphasizes a reason intensifying the result; だけあって emphasizes a result fitting the experience or investment. Both work naturally here; the result being positive or negative does not by itself exclude either.

n2.day4-dake.question.2.anchor.en: A reason that intensifies the result.

n2.day4-dake.question.3.explanation.zh: 「だけに」强调责任重大使小失误更令人介意；「だけあって」可表示这样的反应与重大责任相称。本句两者都自然，因此两项都计分。
n2.day4-dake.question.3.explanation.en: だけに emphasizes how serious responsibility makes small mistakes more concerning. だけあって can present that concern as fitting the responsibility. Both are natural here and are accepted.

n2.day4-dake.question.3.anchor.en: A reason that intensifies the result.

n2.day4-dake.question.4.explanation.zh: 「だけあって」评价结果与十年口译经验相称；「だけに」强调正因为有经验，表达才自然。本句不能仅凭这一重点差异排除另一项，因此两项都计分。
n2.day4-dake.question.4.explanation.en: だけあって evaluates the natural wording as fitting ten years of interpreting experience. だけに emphasizes the experience as the reason. Both are natural in this sentence and are accepted.

n2.day4-dake.question.4.anchor.en: A result that fits the person's experience.

n2.day4-dake.question.5.explanation.zh: 「だけあって」强调队伍很长与人气店的名声相称；「だけに」强调正因为有名，排队的人才多。两种表达在本句均可自然成立，因此两项都计分。
n2.day4-dake.question.5.explanation.en: だけあって presents the long queue as fitting the restaurant's reputation. だけに emphasizes its popularity as the cause. Both are natural in this sentence and are accepted.

n2.day4-dake.question.5.anchor.en: A result that fits the establishment's reputation.

n2.day4-dake.question.6.explanation.zh: 已经看到会话进步，再回头肯定半年的练习没有白费，所以用「だけのことはある」。
n2.day4-dake.question.6.explanation.en: Having seen the progress of the session and being sure that six months of practice have not been wasted, use "だけのことはある " .

n2.day4-dake.question.7.explanation.zh: 服务成果让人觉得这笔高费用确实花得值，强调投入与回报的「だけのことはあって」。 补充：だけに也可强调付费高这一原因；だけのことはあって更像评价“花得值得”。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「だけのことはあって」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day4-dake.question.7.explanation.en: Target expression: だけのことはあって. Intended meaning: An evaluation that the expense was worthwhile. Compared alternatives: だけに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day4-dake.question.7.anchor.en: An evaluation that the expense was worthwhile.

n2.day4-dake.question.8.explanation.zh: 仅仅听到名字这一个条件，就会想起往事；后项已经成立，所以是「だけで」。
n2.day4-dake.question.8.explanation.en: A mere condition of a name reminds me of the past; the latter has been established, so it is "だけで. "

n2.day4-dake.question.9.explanation.zh: 光是听这首歌就能振作起来，A 单独已经足以带来 B。
n2.day4-dake.question.9.explanation.en: Listening to this song alone can cheer up, A alone enough to bring B.

n2.day4-dake.question.10.explanation.zh: 「だけでは」和「だけで」接否定结尾时，都可表示只读说明不足以自然运用。「では」更突出对比其他必要条件；本句两项均计分。
n2.day4-dake.question.10.explanation.en: With the negative ending, both だけでは and だけで can say that merely reading the explanation is insufficient for natural use. では emphasizes comparison with other necessary conditions. Both are accepted.

n2.day4-dake.question.10.anchor.en: The stated condition alone is insufficient.

n2.day4-dake.question.11.explanation.zh: 「だけでは」和「だけで」都可表示仅有天赋不保证成功。「では」使与持续努力等条件的对比更突出；本句两项均计分。
n2.day4-dake.question.11.explanation.en: Both だけでは and だけで can state that talent alone does not guarantee success. では highlights comparison with other conditions, such as sustained effort. Both are accepted.

n2.day4-dake.question.11.anchor.en: The stated condition alone is insufficient.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.anchor.zh: 「最好……」——照我的经验，你就这么做吧。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.anchor.en: “You'd do best to…” — based on my experience, this is what you should do.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.logic.zh: 给对方一条具体建议，语气像过来人叮嘱，不是命令。常出现在「～たいなら」「～悩んでいるなら」之后，回答“那我该怎么办”。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.logic.en: It gives one concrete piece of advice in the voice of someone who has been there, not an order. It usually follows ～たいなら or ～悩んでいるなら, answering so what should I do.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.connection.zh: 动词辞书形／ない形＋ことだ
n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.connection.en: Dictionary form / ない-form + ことだ

n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.contrast.zh: 别和语法上的「～こと」（名词化）混。这里句尾独立成句，是建议。中文先套“最好……”，不要译成“这件事是……”。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.contrast.en: Do not confuse it with the nominaliser ～こと. Here it ends the sentence on its own and gives advice. In Chinese start with 最好 and avoid a literal this matter is.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.translation.zh: 想把日语学好，最好每天都说。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.0.translation.en: If you want to get good at Japanese, talk every day.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.anchor.en: “There's no need to…” — takes the pressure off.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.logic.zh: 告诉对方这个动作不必做，常用于安慰、劝阻、替人宽心。语气轻，不等于禁止，做了也不算错。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.logic.en: It tells the listener the action is unnecessary and is common in reassurance and gentle dissuasion. The tone is light: it is not a ban, and doing it would not be wrong.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋ことはない

n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.contrast.zh: 和「ことだ」正相反：一个劝你做，一个劝你别做。也别读成「てはいけない」——那是禁止，这个是“没必要”。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.contrast.en: It is the mirror image of ことだ: one urges you to do it, the other says you need not. It is also not てはいけない, which forbids, while this merely says there is no need.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.1.translation.en: There is still time, so there is no need to rush.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.anchor.zh: 「以他那性格，肯定……」——靠对一个人的了解来推测。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.anchor.en: “Knowing him, he'll have…” — an inference built on knowing the person.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.logic.zh: 根据某人平时的性格、习惯、处境，推断这次也会做出相符的反应。前项必须是具体的人，后面常接「だろう」「はずだ」「に違いない」。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.logic.en: From someone's usual character, habits or situation, the speaker infers the same reaction this time. What precedes it must be a specific person, and だろう, はずだ or に違いない usually follows.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.connection.zh: 人物名／人称名词＋の＋ことだから
n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.connection.en: Person's name or a personal noun + の + ことだから

n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.contrast.zh: 不是普通的因果「から」。它暗含“他这个人你又不是不知道”，所以只能接人，不能接“因为下雨”。接事物就变回普通原因了。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.contrast.en: It is not an ordinary causal から. It implies you know what he is like, so it takes a person and not something like because it rained. Attach it to a thing and it reverts to a plain reason.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.translation.zh: 以田中那么认真的性格，估计早就准备好了。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.2.translation.en: Tanaka is so diligent that he will have prepared already.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.anchor.zh: 「没……就……」——前项没发生，后项照样进行。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.anchor.en: “Without ever…” — the first action never happens and the second carries on anyway.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.logic.zh: 书面语，报道、文章、正式叙述里常见。常用来突出“一次也没有”“始终没有”，比口语说法更有分量。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.logic.en: A written register found in reports, articles and formal narration. It stresses never once or never at all, which gives it more weight than the spoken equivalent.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.contrast.zh: 口语说「～ないで」。意思接近，但ことなく更正式，写邮件、写报告用它；聊天里用会像在念稿。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.contrast.en: Speech uses ～ないで. The meaning is close, but ことなく is formal and belongs in mail and reports; in conversation it sounds like reading from a script.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.translation.zh: 他什么也没说，就离开了房间。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.3.translation.en: He left the room without saying a word.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.anchor.zh: 「令人……的是」——先给情绪定性，再说事实。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.anchor.en: “To my …” — labels the emotion first, then states the fact.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.logic.zh: 把惊讶、遗憾、庆幸这类反应提到句首，再交代发生了什么。几乎都是固定搭配：驚いたことに、残念なことに、幸いなことに、不思議なことに。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.logic.en: It puts the reaction at the front — surprise, regret, relief — and then reports what happened. The set phrases are almost fixed: 驚いたことに, 残念なことに, 幸いなことに, 不思議なことに.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.connection.zh: い形容词原形／な形容词词干＋な／感情动词た形＋ことに
n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.connection.en: i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な / emotion verb た-form + ことに

n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.contrast.zh: 它不表示目的，也不表示时间。看到「ことに」在句首、后面紧跟逗号，就当“令人……的是”；看到「～ことにしている」才是习惯。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.contrast.en: It marks neither purpose nor time. When ことに opens the clause and a comma follows, read it as to my …; only ～ことにしている means a personal habit.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.translation.zh: 令人吃惊的是，他一个人全做完了。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.4.translation.en: To my surprise, he finished the whole thing alone.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.anchor.zh: 「不知道有多……啊」——情绪大到说不出具体程度。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.anchor.en: “How … it was!” — the feeling is too big for a plain degree word.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.logic.zh: 用反问的外形表达强烈感叹，句尾虽然有「か」，却不是在等人回答。常与「どんなに」「どれほど」「何度」呼应，多出现在回忆和抒情段落。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.logic.en: It wears the shape of a question but expresses strong emotion, and the か at the end waits for no answer. It usually pairs with どんなに, どれほど or 何度 and belongs to reminiscence and lyrical passages.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.connection.zh: 普通形＋ことか（な形容词・名词＋な＋ことか）
n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.connection.en: Plain form + ことか (na-adjective / noun + な + ことか)

n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.contrast.zh: 别当成疑问句去回答。中文若译成“有多高兴呢？”，读者会以为在提问；应译“不知道有多高兴”。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.contrast.en: Do not treat it as a question to be answered. Rendering it as how happy was it? makes readers expect a reply; the sense is I cannot tell you how happy I was.

n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.translation.zh: 合格的时候，不知道有多高兴。
n2.day5-koto.grammar.5.translation.en: You cannot imagine how happy I was when I passed.

n2.day5-koto.question.0.explanation.zh: 这是根据情况给建议：想恢复身体，今晚最好好好休息，因此用「ことだ」。
n2.day5-koto.question.0.explanation.en: This is a recommendation based on the situation: it is better to get some rest tonight if you want to get well, so use "ことだ " .

n2.day5-koto.question.1.explanation.zh: 后项是对学习方法的建议，中文自然地说“最好试着开口说”。
n2.day5-koto.question.1.explanation.en: The latter is a proposal for learning methods, and Chinese naturally says “it is best to try to speak out”.

n2.day5-koto.question.2.explanation.zh: 说话人在安慰对方：只失败一次，用不着那么消沉。
n2.day5-koto.question.2.explanation.en: Those who spoke comforted each other: it was only once that they failed, and there was no need to be so depressed.

n2.day5-koto.question.3.explanation.zh: 离截止还有一周，没有现在立刻熬夜的必要，所以用「ことはない」。
n2.day5-koto.question.3.explanation.en: One week from now, there is no need to stay up at night, so use "ことはない " .

n2.day5-koto.question.4.explanation.zh: 根据对他责任感强这一性格的了解作推测，用「彼のことだから」。
n2.day5-koto.question.4.explanation.en: The inference is based on knowing his strong sense of responsibility. Use 彼のことだから.

n2.day5-koto.question.5.explanation.zh: 以佐藤一向守时的性格来推测他已经到了，是典型人物判断。
n2.day5-koto.question.5.explanation.en: It's typical to assume that Sato has arrived by his time-honoured character.

n2.day5-koto.question.6.explanation.zh: 一次也没有放弃，一直跑到最后；正式书面表达用「ことなく」。
n2.day5-koto.question.6.explanation.en: Never gave up, never left; officially expressed in writing by " ことなく. "

n2.day5-koto.question.7.explanation.zh: 没有说明理由就离开了，前项未发生而后项继续，用「ことなく」。
n2.day5-koto.question.7.explanation.en: He left without a reason, the previous one did not occur and the latter continued with " ことなく " .

n2.day5-koto.question.8.explanation.zh: 先给后面的事实加“惊讶”标签，固定表达是「驚いたことに」。
n2.day5-koto.question.8.explanation.en: 驚いたことに introduces the following fact as surprising.

n2.day5-koto.question.9.explanation.zh: 对“无人受伤”先作幸运评价，用「幸いなことに」。
n2.day5-koto.question.9.explanation.en: "No one gets hurt" was first evaluated by "幸いなことに".

n2.day5-koto.question.10.explanation.zh: 「どれほど」与「ことか」呼应，强烈感叹自己等这一天等了很久。
n2.day5-koto.question.10.explanation.en: "どれほど" echoes "ことか" and strongly laments that he has waited for this day for a long time.

n2.day5-koto.question.11.explanation.zh: 不是疑问，而是感叹当时不知道有多不安，所以选「ことか」。
n2.day5-koto.question.11.explanation.en: It was not a question, but an exaggeration that I didn't know how uneasy it was, so I chose "ことか".

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.anchor.zh: 「正要……」——镜头定格在动作开始前的一刻。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.anchor.en: “About to…” — the camera stops just before the action starts.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.logic.zh: 动作还没开始，但已经走到启动的节点。常和「今から」「ちょうど今」搭配，回答“你在干什么”。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.logic.en: The action has not begun but is at the starting line. It often pairs with 今から or ちょうど今 and answers what are you doing.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.contrast.zh: 普通未来只说之后会做；「ところだ」把时间压到“就在这一刻”。中文的“要去了”有时只是打算，日文这里是真的马上动身。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.contrast.en: A plain future only says it will happen later; ところだ squeezes the time down to this very moment. Chinese 要去了 can be a mere plan, while this really means leaving right now.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.0.translation.en: I am just about to go out.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.anchor.zh: 「正在……呢」——动作进行到一半，人还在里面。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.anchor.en: “In the middle of…” — the action is under way right now.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.logic.zh: 强调此刻所处的阶段，常用来回应打扰或说明进度。比单纯的「～ています」更有“正做到这儿”的现场感。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.logic.en: It stresses the stage the speaker is at, often to answer an interruption or report progress. It feels more live than a plain ～ています.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.connection.zh: 动词ている形＋ところだ
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.connection.en: ている form + ところだ

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.contrast.zh: 「～ています」也能说正在做，但那是状态；「ところだ」是在报告进度。电话里说“正在开会”用后者更自然。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.contrast.en: ～ています also says it is happening, but as a state; ところだ reports progress. On the phone, saying you are in a meeting sounds more natural with the latter.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.1.translation.en: We are looking into the cause right now.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.2.anchor.en: “Just finished…” — the action has only just ended.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.2.logic.zh: 说话人把动作看成“完成后不久”的状态，常和「今」「さっき」搭配。用于报告刚到、刚做完、刚听说。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.2.logic.en: The speaker treats the action as having ended a moment ago, usually with 今 or さっき. It reports having just arrived, just finished or just heard.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.2.contrast.zh: 不要和「Vたところ、B」混。句末有「だ」是刚做完；后面还接一个结果句，才是“做了以后发现”。看逗号后面有没有 B。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.2.contrast.en: Do not confuse it with Vたところ、B. A だ at the end means just finished; a result clause after the comma means did it and found. Look at what follows the comma.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.2.translation.en: I have just arrived at the office.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.anchor.zh: 「一……结果发现……」——做了才知道，事前并不确定。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.anchor.en: “I did …, and it turned out…” — the result was unknown until the action was taken.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.logic.zh: 实际做了 A 之后，得到 B 这个结果或发现，B 往往是意外消息。常见于调查、询问、尝试之后的汇报。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.logic.en: After actually doing A, the speaker obtains result B, which is often unexpected news. It appears in reports after checking, asking or trying.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词た形＋ところ、结果句
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.connection.en: た-form + ところ + result clause

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.contrast.zh: 和「たところだ」只差一个逗号，意思完全不同：一个是刚做完，一个是做完之后发现。考试常把两句并排放在一起考。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.contrast.en: Only a comma separates it from たところだ, yet the meaning is entirely different: one is just finished, the other is did it and found. Exams like to place the two side by side.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.translation.zh: 去医院检查了一下，结果没发现什么问题。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.3.translation.en: I had the hospital check it, and there was nothing wrong.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.anchor.zh: 「差点就……」——事没发生，人还在后怕。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.anchor.en: “Nearly…” — it did not happen, and the speaker is still shaken.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.logic.zh: 和「危うく」「もう少しで」一起用，表示险些发生而实际避开了。句尾几乎固定为「ところだった」。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.logic.en: Used with 危うく or もう少しで, it means something almost happened but was avoided. The ending is almost always ところだった.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.connection.zh: 动词辞书形＋ところだった
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.connection.en: Dictionary form + ところだった

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.contrast.zh: 不加「危うく」时可能只是回顾“那时正要出门”，不能一口咬定结果如何。有「危うく」「もう少しで」才是“差点”。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.contrast.en: Without 危うく it may simply recall being about to leave, and says nothing about how it turned out. Only with 危うく or もう少しで does it mean nearly.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.4.translation.en: I very nearly left my wallet behind.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.anchor.zh: 「正当……的时候，偏偏……」——A 到关键处，B 插进来。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.anchor.en: “Just as … , along came…” — right at the critical moment, B cuts in.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.logic.zh: 正在做 A 的那个节点上，另一个人、动作或事件突然出现。常和「～ようとしていた」「～ている」搭配，后半句多是打断或意外。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.logic.en: At the very point of doing A, another person, action or event appears. It pairs with ～ようとしていた or ～ている, and the second half is usually an interruption or a surprise.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.connection.zh: 动词辞书形・ている形・ようとしている＋ところに／へ
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.connection.en: Dictionary, ている or ようとしている form + ところに or ところへ

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.contrast.zh: 「に」强调事件落在这个时点，「へ」带“朝这边过来”的方向感。别把它读成描述 A 的阶段——它真正的任务是引出 B。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.contrast.en: に places the event at that moment while へ adds a sense of movement toward the speaker. Do not read it as describing A's stage — its real job is to bring in B.

n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.translation.zh: 正准备出门的时候，偏偏下起雨来了。
n2.day6-tokoro.grammar.5.translation.en: Just as I was about to leave, it started to rain.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.0.explanation.zh: 「今から」说明动作尚未开始、马上开始，辞书形＋ところ表示正要吃。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.0.explanation.en: 今から indicates that the action has not started but is about to. Dictionary form + ところ describes being about to eat.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.1.explanation.zh: 会议还没开始，但马上准备开始，是开始前一刻的「Vるところ」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.1.explanation.en: The meeting has not yet begun, but it is now ready to begin with the "V るところ " .

n2.day6-tokoro.question.2.explanation.zh: 「確認しているところ」强调负责人此时此刻正处于确认过程中。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.2.explanation.en: 確認しているところ emphasizes that the person in charge is checking at this very moment.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.3.explanation.zh: 正在与客人交谈，动作进行中，用「Vているところ」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.3.explanation.en: Talking to guests, moving in with "V ているところ".

n2.day6-tokoro.question.4.explanation.zh: 「さっき」与句末「Vたところです」一起表示刚到车站。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.4.explanation.en: さっき and the end of the sentence "V たところです" indicate that we have just arrived at the station.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.5.explanation.zh: 邮件动作才刚完成，句末用「Vたところだ」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.5.explanation.en: The mail action has just been completed. At the end of the sentence, use "V たところだ".

n2.day6-tokoro.question.6.explanation.zh: 实际去问以后，得到老师马上说明这一结果，用「Vたところ、B」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.6.explanation.en: When actually asked, the teacher explained the result, using "V たところ, B " .

n2.day6-tokoro.question.7.explanation.zh: 去了以后才发现已经关门，重点是行动后得到的意外结果。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.7.explanation.en: After that, it was discovered that the doors were closed, with emphasis on the unintended results obtained after the operation.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.8.explanation.zh: 「もう少しで」说明最终没有摔倒，但险些发生，用「Vるところだった」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.8.explanation.en: もう少しで indicates that the fall was narrowly avoided. Use Vるところだった for something that almost happened.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.9.explanation.zh: 幸好刹车才没有撞上，是已经逼近却未发生的「ところだった」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.9.explanation.en: Fortunately, the brakes didn't hit it. It was "ところだった", which was close but never happened.

n2.day6-tokoro.question.10.explanation.zh: 正准备出门这个节点，快递突然到来；新事件插入用「ところに」。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.10.explanation.en: Preparations are under way for this node, and the courier arrives suddenly; new events are inserted with "ところに " .

n2.day6-tokoro.question.11.explanation.zh: 大家正吃饭时，迟到的朋友朝这里来了；有明显移动方向，使用「ところへ」很自然。
n2.day6-tokoro.question.11.explanation.en: As you eat, your late friends come in this direction; there is a clear movement and it is natural to use " ところへ. "

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.anchor.en: “While…” — the window is still open, so do it now.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.logic.zh: 某种有利状态以后可能会变，所以在它还保持的时候主动完成一件事。后项多是计划、建议或决心，带紧迫感。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.logic.en: A favourable state may not last, so the speaker acts while it does. The second half is usually a plan, a suggestion or a resolve, with a sense of urgency.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.connection.zh: 动词辞书形・ている形／い形容词／な形容词＋な／名词＋の＋うちに
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.connection.en: Dictionary or ている form / i-adjective / na-adjective + な / noun + の + うちに

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.contrast.zh: 别机械译成“在……里面”。后项是主动计划或劝人行动时，中文先说“趁着”。译成“在日本里”就读不通了。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.contrast.en: Do not render it mechanically as 在……里面. When the second half is a plan or a nudge to act, Chinese starts with 趁着; 在日本里 would be unreadable.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.translation.zh: 趁还在日本，想去一趟北海道。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.0.translation.en: While I am still in Japan, I want to visit Hokkaido.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.1.anchor.en: “Before it…” — once the change comes, it is too late.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.1.logic.zh: 不希望发生的变化还没出现，趁这个空档及时行动。常用于备忘、提醒、劝告，句尾多接「～ておこう」「～たほうがいい」。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.1.logic.en: An unwanted change has not yet arrived, so the speaker acts in the gap. It is common in notes, reminders and advice, often with ～ておこう or ～たほうがいい.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.1.contrast.zh: 和「前に」比，它多一层“随时会变”的紧迫。说“趁还没忘”用ないうちに，说“开会前”用前に，后者只是时间顺序。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.1.contrast.en: Compared with 前に it adds the urgency of a change that may come at any moment. Before I forget takes ないうちに, while before the meeting takes 前に, which is only sequence.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.1.translation.en: Let me write it down before I forget.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.anchor.zh: 「……着……着，不知不觉就……」——没人刻意，变化自己来了。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.anchor.en: “… and before I knew it…” — nobody tried, yet the change happened on its own.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.logic.zh: A 一直持续，在这个过程中 B 自然而然地发生了。B 多是能力、心情、习惯这类慢慢转变的东西，句尾常接「～ようになった」。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.logic.en: A goes on and on, and somewhere in the middle B happens by itself. B is usually a slow shift in ability, feeling or habit, often closed with ～ようになった.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.connection.en: ている form + うちに

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.contrast.zh: 同样是「うちに」，这一种不是“趁机主动做”。后项若是能力、心情、习惯的自然变化，就要读成“……着……着就……”，别译成“趁着”。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.contrast.en: It is the same うちに, but this one is not about seizing a chance. When the second half is a natural shift in ability, feeling or habit, read it as and before I knew it, not as while I still can.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.translation.zh: 日语学着学着，慢慢也对日本文化产生兴趣了。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.2.translation.en: As I studied Japanese, I gradually became interested in Japanese culture too.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.anchor.en: “As long as…” — for the whole stretch of time.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.logic.zh: 前项状态持续的整段时间里，后项的判断、习惯或情况一直成立。后项多是持续性的说法，如「～つもりだ」「～ている」。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.logic.en: Throughout the period in which the first state holds, the judgement, habit or situation in the second half holds too. The second half is usually durative, such as ～つもりだ or ～ている.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词辞书形・ている形／い形容词／な形容词＋な／名词＋の＋うちは
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.connection.en: Dictionary or ている form / i-adjective / na-adjective + な / noun + の + うちは

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.contrast.zh: 「うちに」盯的是改变前的某一刻，「うちは」说的是从头到尾整段。中文先判断：是“趁现在”，还是“只要还”。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.contrast.en: うちに watches one moment before a change, while うちは covers the whole stretch. In Chinese, decide first whether it is while I still can or as long as.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.translation.zh: 只要还在日本，我就打算继续学日语。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.3.translation.en: As long as I am in Japan, I intend to keep studying Japanese.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.anchor.zh: 「在……当中」——先划一个圈子，再在圈里比较。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.anchor.en: “Among…” — draw a circle first, then compare inside it.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.logic.zh: 把若干人或物组成一个范围，在这个范围内作比较或下判断，常和「いちばん」「最も」搭配。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.logic.en: It gathers people or things into a set and judges within it, often with いちばん or 最も.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.contrast.zh: 「うちは」谈时间或状态的持续，「うちでは」谈集合范围。看到「いちばん」这种比较词，基本就是「うちでは」。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.contrast.en: うちは is about time or a continuing state, while うちでは is about a set. When you see a comparison word such as いちばん, it is almost certainly うちでは.

n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.translation.zh: 在这三个人当中，田中最年轻。
n2.day7-uchi.grammar.4.translation.en: Of the three, Tanaka is the youngest.

n2.day7-uchi.question.0.explanation.zh: 以后可能离开日本，所以想趁还在日本时主动去北海道，用「うちに」。 补充：うちは也能限定身在日本的时期；うちに更突出趁机会实现一次愿望。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「うちに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day7-uchi.question.0.explanation.en: Target expression: うちに. Intended meaning: Taking a one-time opportunity before the situation changes. Compared alternatives: うちは. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day7-uchi.question.0.anchor.en: Taking a one-time opportunity before the situation changes.

n2.day7-uchi.question.1.explanation.zh: 食物的热度会改变，要趁热吃，是状态变化前主动行动的「うちに」。 补充：うちは可强调只在热的时候吃；趁没凉赶紧吃的邀请通常用うちに。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「うちに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day7-uchi.question.1.explanation.en: Target expression: うちに. Intended meaning: Taking action before a favorable state changes. Compared alternatives: うちは. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day7-uchi.question.1.anchor.en: Taking action before a favorable state changes.

n2.day7-uchi.question.2.explanation.zh: 趁还没有忘记先写下来，直接使用「忘れないうちに」。
n2.day7-uchi.question.2.explanation.en: Write it down before forgetting. Use 忘れないうちに.

n2.day7-uchi.question.3.explanation.zh: 雨随时可能下，要趁还没下雨回家，用「降らないうちに」。
n2.day7-uchi.question.3.explanation.en: Rain could start at any moment, so return home before it does. Use 降らないうちに.

n2.day7-uchi.question.4.explanation.zh: 持续使用的过程中自然而然习惯了操作，不是刻意“趁着”做某事。
n2.day7-uchi.question.4.explanation.en: It is natural to get used to it in the course of its continued use, not to do something deliberately “while”.

n2.day7-uchi.question.5.explanation.zh: 反复听着听着，理解歌词的能力逐渐产生，是过程中的自然变化。
n2.day7-uchi.question.5.explanation.en: The ability to listen repeatedly and understand the lyrics is a natural change in the process.

n2.day7-uchi.question.6.explanation.zh: 说的是整个年轻时期都成立的判断，不是劝人趁年轻完成某个动作，因此用「うちは」。
n2.day7-uchi.question.6.explanation.en: It is a young judgement that has been established throughout the youth, not to persuade people to do something while they are young, so use " うちは " .

n2.day7-uchi.question.6.anchor.en: As long as it's still... / During...

n2.day7-uchi.question.7.explanation.zh: 只要父母还健康，每年一起旅行这一愿望就持续成立，强调整个期间。
n2.day7-uchi.question.7.explanation.en: As long as the parents are healthy, the desire to travel together every year is sustained, with emphasis on the entire period.

n2.day7-uchi.question.7.anchor.en: As long as it's still... / During...

n2.day7-uchi.question.8.explanation.zh: 先划出三个方案的范围，再在其中比较哪个最容易实现，用「三つの案のうちでは」。
n2.day7-uchi.question.8.explanation.en: Define the three proposals as the comparison group, then compare their feasibility. Use 三つの案のうちでは.

n2.day7-uchi.question.9.explanation.zh: 在班级学生这一范围中作比较，最自然的是「学生のうちでは」。
n2.day7-uchi.question.9.explanation.en: For a comparison within the group of students, 学生のうちでは is most natural.

n2.day7-uchi.question.10.explanation.zh: 聊天过程中不知不觉到了末班车时间，是持续过程中自然发生的变化。
n2.day7-uchi.question.10.explanation.en: The end of the bus, undetected during the chat, is a natural change in the continuation process.

n2.day7-uchi.question.11.explanation.zh: 健康状态以后可能改变，因此想趁身体还好时主动去想去的地方，用「うちに」。 补充：うちは侧重身体仍健康的时期；うちに更突出趁现在抓紧实现愿望。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「うちに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day7-uchi.question.11.explanation.en: Target expression: うちに. Intended meaning: Taking opportunities before the current favorable state changes. Compared alternatives: うちは. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day7-uchi.question.11.anchor.en: Taking opportunities before the current favorable state changes.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.anchor.zh: 「虽说……可是……」——承认前半句，平静地摆出相反的事实。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.anchor.en: “Granted…, but…” — concedes the first half and calmly sets down a contrary fact.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.logic.zh: 逆接这一组的基准项：先把 A 认下来，再客观补上与预想不一致的 B，不带情绪。文章、报告里最稳妥的写法。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.logic.en: The baseline of the concession group: accept A, then objectively add the unexpected B with no feeling attached. It is the safest choice in articles and reports.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.connection.zh: 动词・い形容词普通形／な形容词词干＋な・である／名词＋である＋ものの
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.connection.en: Verb or i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な or である / noun + である + ものの

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.contrast.zh: 和这一组其他成员比：比「にもかかわらず」冷静，没有“怎么会这样”的惊讶；也没有「くせに」的责怪。想表达不满时用错了会显得很别扭。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.contrast.en: Compared with the rest of the group it is calmer than にもかかわらず, with none of the how could this be, and free of the blame in くせに. Using it to complain reads awkwardly.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.translation.zh: 虽说在日本住了很久，可敬语还是不太擅长。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.0.translation.en: I have lived in Japan a long time, but keigo still defeats me.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.anchor.zh: 「虽然……但还是……」——两头都认，重点是并存的矛盾。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.anchor.en: “Even though…” — both sides stand, and the contradiction is the point.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.logic.zh: 前项是事实，后项与通常预期不同。既可正面评价（小さいながらも便利だ），也可批评（知っていながらも教えない），不是只能写“克服困难”。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.logic.en: The first half is a fact and the second departs from expectation. It can praise (小さいながらも便利だ) or criticise (知っていながらも教えない); it is not reserved for overcoming hardship.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.connection.zh: 动词ます形去ます／い形容词原形／な形容词词干／名词＋ながらも
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.connection.en: Verb masu-stem / i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem / noun + ながらも

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.contrast.zh: 接续最容易错：动词要用ます形去ます或「てい」，不能直接接た形。另外别只记“虽然有困难却努力”，那是常见语境，不是词义。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.contrast.en: The connection trips people up: verbs take the masu-stem or てい, never the た-form directly. Also do not reduce it to struggling on despite hardship — that is a common setting, not the meaning.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.translation.zh: 虽然是家小公司，技术实力却很强。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.1.translation.en: Small as it is, the company has strong technical skills.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.anchor.zh: 「尽管……居然还是……」——预期被硬生生打破。

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.logic.zh: 按常理 A 应该导致某个结果，实际却反向发生。惊讶和强调都在“违背预期”上，书面语色彩强。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.logic.en: By any normal reckoning A should lead somewhere, yet the opposite happens. The surprise and the emphasis sit on the broken expectation, and the register is written.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.connection.zh: 普通形／名词＋にもかかわらず（な形容词・名词可用である）
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.connection.en: Plain form / noun + にもかかわらず (na-adjectives and nouns may take である)

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.contrast.zh: 和「ものの」的差别在情绪强度：「ものの」只是并列两个事实，「にもかかわらず」是“明明不该这样，结果居然”。客观陈述用前者，强调反常才用后者。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.contrast.en: The difference from ものの is emotional force: ものの merely sets two facts side by side, while にもかかわらず says this should not have happened and yet it did. Use the first for neutral reporting and the second to stress the anomaly.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.translation.zh: 尽管下着大雨，居然还是来了很多人。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.2.translation.en: Despite the heavy rain, a great many people came.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.anchor.en: “And yet you…” — reproachful, looking down on someone.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.logic.zh: 说话人认定对方的 A 与 B 明显矛盾，对这种言行不一表示不满、责怪甚至轻蔑。多用于说别人，说自己时带自嘲。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.logic.en: The speaker finds A and B plainly inconsistent and reacts with displeasure, blame or contempt. It usually targets other people and reads as self-mockery when turned on oneself.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词・い形容词普通形／な形容词词干＋な／名词＋の＋くせに
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.connection.en: Verb or i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な / noun + の + くせに

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.contrast.zh: な形容词接くせに时要加な（静かなくせに），不是否定形的なく，这一点最容易写错。另外当面说人很冒犯，正式场合一律换成「ものの」。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.contrast.en: A na-adjective takes な before くせに, as in 静かなくせに, not the negative なく — that is the mistake people make most. Said to someone's face it is offensive, so formal settings want ものの instead.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.translation.zh: 明明不知道，却还装作知道。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.3.translation.en: He does not know, yet he pretends he does.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.anchor.zh: 「按这个程度来说，倒是……」——拿程度当尺子量结果。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.anchor.en: “For how … it is, surprisingly…” — measures the result against a degree.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.logic.zh: 把 A 的程度、价格、投入或一般印象当尺子，发现 B 与这把尺子不成比例，常带轻微意外。尺子可以很宽泛。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.logic.en: A's degree, price, outlay or general impression serves as the ruler, and B turns out out of proportion to it, usually with mild surprise. The ruler can be quite loose.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.connection.zh: 普通形＋わりに（な形容词＋なわりに；名词＋のわりに）
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.connection.en: Plain form + わりに (na-adjective + なわりに; noun + のわりに)

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.contrast.zh: 和「にしては」都译“按……来说”，区别在尺子：わりに的尺子是模糊的程度或印象，にしては的尺子是明确的条件——新人、半年、孩子、这个价钱。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.contrast.en: Both render as 按……来说, but the ruler differs: わりに uses a vague degree or impression, while にしては uses a definite condition such as a newcomer, six months, a child or this price.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.translation.zh: 这家店按价格这么便宜来说，味道倒是很好。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.4.translation.en: For how cheap this place is, the food is remarkably good.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.anchor.zh: 「按……这个条件来说，居然……」——基准很具体。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.anchor.en: “For a … , that's surprisingly…” — the benchmark is concrete.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.logic.zh: 先把 A 当成明确基准，再说 B 高于或低于这个基准下的一般预期。基准多是身份、年龄、时间、经验、价格这类可以点数的事。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.logic.en: A is set as a definite benchmark, and B is judged above or below what that benchmark would lead you to expect. The benchmark is usually something countable: status, age, time, experience, price.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.connection.zh: 名词／普通形＋にしては（尤常接身份、年龄、时间、经验等基准）
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.connection.en: Noun / plain form + にしては (often status, age, time or experience)

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.contrast.zh: 判断时先自问：“我是不是在拿新人、半年、孩子这种具体条件当标准？”是就用「にしては」，只是笼统觉得“不太相称”就用「わりに」。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.contrast.en: Ask yourself whether you are measuring against a concrete condition such as a newcomer, six months or a child. If so, use にしては; if the mismatch is only a vague impression, use わりに.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.translation.zh: 按来日本才半年这个条件来说，日语居然已经这么好了。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.grammar.5.translation.en: For someone who has been in Japan only six months, his Japanese is very good.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.0.explanatio.zh: 只是客观地说“住了很久，但敬语仍不擅长”，没有责怪对方，用「ものの」。 补充：くせに会带责备（若说自己则自嘲）；にしては按在日经历作比较。ものの较中性。住んでいる不能直接接ながらも，要用住んでいながらも。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ものの」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.0.explanatio.en: Target expression: ものの. Intended meaning: A neutral acknowledgment followed by a contrasting fact, without blame or comparison. Compared alternatives: くせに / にしては. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.0.anchor.en: A neutral acknowledgment followed by a contrasting fact, without blame or comparison.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.1.explanatio.zh: 先承认已经开始新工作，再冷静补充仍不知该做什么，是中性转折的「ものの」。 补充：这几项都能形成转折；ものの承认现状，にもかかわらず突出反预期，わりに作程度比较，くせに带责备。原句没有足够信息将它们判为语法错误。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ものの」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.1.explanatio.en: Target expression: ものの. Intended meaning: A neutral acknowledgment followed by a contrasting fact, without blame or comparison. Compared alternatives: にもかかわらず / わりに / くせに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.1.anchor.en: A neutral acknowledgment followed by a contrasting fact, without blame or comparison.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.2.explanatio.zh: 规模小是不利条件，但依然在海外获得高评价；肯定逆风中的成果，用「ながらも」。 补充：会社にしては按公司规模作比较，也成立。名词若用くせに／ものの需改变接续，如会社のくせに／会社であるものの。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ながらも」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.2.explanatio.en: Target expression: ながらも. Intended meaning: Acknowledging an unfavorable condition while affirming an achievement. Compared alternatives: にしては. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.2.anchor.en: Acknowledging an unfavorable condition while affirming an achievement.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.3.explanatio.zh: 年轻可能意味着经验有限，但他仍然有统筹团队的能力，「若いながらも」接续也正确。 补充：若いわりに、若いものの、若いにもかかわらず都可以表达年龄与能力的反预期，语体与评价重点不同。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ながらも」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.3.explanatio.en: Target expression: ながらも. Intended meaning: Acknowledging an unfavorable condition while affirming an ability. Compared alternatives: わりに / ものの / にもかかわらず. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.3.anchor.en: Acknowledging an unfavorable condition while affirming an ability.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.4.explanatio.zh: 按常理大雨会让来的人变少，实际却来了很多人，强调违背预期用「にもかかわらず」。 补充：大雨にしては按天气作比较；大雨ながらも也可转折。にもかかわらず更直接强调不顾恶劣条件仍到场。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「にもかかわらず」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.4.explanatio.en: Target expression: にもかかわらず. Intended meaning: Emphasizing a result contrary to expectations despite an obstacle. Compared alternatives: にしては / ながらも. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.4.anchor.en: Emphasizing a result contrary to expectations despite an obstacle.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.5.explanatio.zh: 充分准备本应带来合格，结果却落榜，这种强烈的反预期最符合「にもかかわらず」。 补充：ものの较中性，くせに可含批评或自嘲，わりに比较投入与结果。准备过却落榜可用不同态度叙述。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「にもかかわらず」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.5.explanatio.en: Target expression: にもかかわらず. Intended meaning: Emphasizing a result contrary to expectations despite preparation. Compared alternatives: ものの / くせに / わりに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.5.anchor.en: Emphasizing a result contrary to expectations despite preparation.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.6.explanatio.zh: 自己也迟到却责怪别人，说话人明显在批评这种矛盾行为，用带不满的「くせに」。 补充：ものの较中性地转折；にしては也能把他自己迟到这一事实作为评价基准。くせに最直接责备其双重标准。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「くせに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.6.explanatio.en: Target expression: くせに. Intended meaning: Blaming someone for contradictory behavior. Compared alternatives: ものの / にしては. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.7.explanatio.zh: 对“不知道却装知道”的人表达不满和责怪，不是冷静地陈述反差。 补充：くせに责备最强；わりに、にもかかわらず、ものの也可表达知之甚少与装懂之间的反差，不能一律判错。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「くせに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.7.explanatio.en: Target expression: くせに. Intended meaning: Blaming someone for pretending to know. Compared alternatives: わりに / にもかかわらず / ものの. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.7.anchor.en: Blaming someone for pretending to know.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.8.explanatio.zh: 「安いわりに」和「安いにしては」在本句中都能自然地以价格为基准比较性能，因此两项都计分。「くせに」增加随意的评价或惊讶语气；「ながらも」侧重逆接，和本题要求的比较重点不同。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.8.explanatio.en: Both 安いわりに and 安いにしては naturally compare performance with expectations based on price, so both are accepted. くせに adds a casual evaluative tone; ながらも presents a concession rather than the comparison requested here.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.8.anchor.en: Comparing performance with expectations based on price.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.9.explanatio.zh: 「よく勉強するわりに」和「よく勉強するにしては」在本句中都能自然地以学习量为基准比较成绩，因此两项都计分。「ものの」是较中性的逆接；「にもかかわらず」强调反预期，与比较的重点不同。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.9.explanatio.en: Both よく勉強するわりに and よく勉強するにしては naturally compare results with effort, so both are accepted. ものの states a neutral concession; にもかかわらず emphasizes a result contrary to expectations. Their focus differs from the requested comparison.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.9.anchor.en: Comparing results with the amount of effort.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.10.explanati.zh: 「日本に来て一年にしては」按来日一年的经验作评价。名词后的わりに、くせに需要の，不能直接接；につれて表示伴随变化，不合本句。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.10.explanati.en: 日本に来て一年にしては evaluates someone against the experience expected after one year in Japan. After a noun, わりに and くせに require の. につれて expresses accompanying change and does not fit here.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.10.anchor.zh: 按这个身份/条件来说，居然……

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.11.explanati.zh: “新人”是一个明确的身份基准，工作上手速度超出了对新人的一般预期，用「にしては」。 补充：新人にもかかわらず也能强调反预期；にしては重在新人这一评价标准。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「にしては」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.11.explanati.en: Target expression: にしては. Intended meaning: Judging a result against expectations for a stated status. Compared alternatives: にもかかわらず. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.11.anchor.zh: 按这个身份/条件来说，居然……
n2.day8-gyakusetsu.question.11.anchor.en: Judging a result against expectations for a stated status.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.anchor.zh: 「因为……导致……」——客观交代成因，落在已经发生的结果上。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.anchor.en: “Owing to…” — states a cause objectively, with a result that has already happened.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.logic.zh: 新闻、说明文、报告里最常用的因果表达。后项多是事实结果：延迟、中止、死亡、增加，而不是说话人的请求或打算。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.logic.en: The most common causal expression in news, explanations and reports. The second half is usually a factual result such as a delay, a cancellation, a death or an increase, not a request or a plan.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.connection.zh: 动词普通形／い形容词／な形容词＋な／名词＋の＋ため（に）
n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.connection.en: Verb plain form / i-adjective / na-adjective + な / noun + の + ため（に）

n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.contrast.zh: 同一个「ために」还能表目的。分辨方法：后项是自己主动做的准备就是“为了”，是已经发生的事实就是“因为”。看结果有没有意志。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.contrast.en: The same ために also marks purpose. To tell them apart: if the second half is preparation someone deliberately makes, it means in order to; if it is a fact that has already happened, it means because. Look for intention in the result.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.translation.zh: 因为下大雪，电车晚点了。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.0.translation.en: The trains were delayed because of heavy snow.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.anchor.zh: 「因为……嘛」——当事人自己交代理由，带辩解味。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.anchor.en: “Because…, you see” — the person involved explains, with a note of excuse.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.logic.zh: 放在原因这一组里，它的特点是“我也有苦衷”。口语里常说成「もんだから」，后半句多是道歉或推脱。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.logic.en: Within the cause group its speciality is that the speaker has a grievance of their own. In speech it often becomes もんだから, and the second half is usually an apology or an excuse.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.connection.zh: 普通形＋ものだから（な形容词・名词＋な＋ものだから）
n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.connection.en: Plain form + ものだから (na-adjective / noun + な + ものだから)

n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.contrast.zh: 和「ために」正相反：ために像新闻稿，ものだから像当事人在解释。写报告用ために，跟朋友解释迟到用ものだから。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.contrast.en: It is the opposite of ために: ために reads like a news item, ものだから like the person explaining themselves. Use ために in a report and ものだから when explaining lateness to a friend.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.translation.zh: 因为电车停运了嘛，所以才迟到。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.1.translation.en: The trains had stopped, so I ended up late.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.anchor.zh: 「就因为……结果倒霉了」——单一原因捅出坏结果。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.anchor.en: “All because…” — one small cause brings a bad outcome.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.logic.zh: A 看似不起眼，却成了坏结果 B 的导火索。说话人常带后悔：早知道就不那样。后项原则上是负面结果。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.logic.en: A looks trivial but sets off the bad result B. The speaker usually regrets it, wishing they had not done it. The second half is in principle negative.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.connection.zh: 普通形＋ばかりに（な形容词＋な；名词＋である）
n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.connection.en: Plain form + ばかりに (na-adjective + な; noun + である)

n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.contrast.zh: 关键不是普通因果，而是“偏偏就因这一件事吃了亏”。用来说好结果会不自然。也别和「だけに」混——那个是“更……”，好坏都行。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.contrast.en: The point is not ordinary causation but that this one thing and no other caused the loss. With a good result it sounds wrong. Do not confuse it with だけに, which means all the more and works either way.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.translation.zh: 就因为多嘴说了一句，结果把他惹火了。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.2.translation.en: One careless remark was all it took to make him angry.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.anchor.zh: 「正因为……所以更……」——前项越重，后项越明显。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.anchor.en: “Precisely because…” — the heavier the cause, the sharper the effect.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.logic.zh: A 的程度、期待或特别性把 B 推得更高。它不只交代原因，更是在说“正因为如此，才格外……”。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.logic.en: A's degree, expectation or specialness pushes B higher. It does more than give a cause: it says that precisely for this reason the effect is all the greater.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.connection.zh: 动词・い形容词普通形／な形容词词干＋な／名词＋だけに（な形容词・名词也可用である）
n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.connection.en: Verb or i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な / noun + だけに (na-adjectives and nouns may also take である)

n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.contrast.zh: 这是 Day 4 的复习点。「ばかりに」是单一原因带来坏结果；「だけに」是前项让后项“更……”，好坏都能用。两个都带「に」，但方向完全不同。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.contrast.en: This revisits Day 4. ばかりに has one cause producing a bad result; だけに has the cause making the effect stronger, good or bad. Both end in に but they point in different directions.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.translation.zh: 正因为一直很期待，取消时才格外失望。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.3.translation.en: I had looked forward to it so much that the cancellation hurt all the more.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.anchor.zh: 「从……来看／因……而得名」——把线索或由来摆出来。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.anchor.en: “Judging from… / so named because…” — sets out the clue or the origin.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.logic.zh: 两种用法都基于同一件事：A 是判断 B 的依据，或者 A 是某个称呼、习惯的由来。常见于说明文、词源介绍、观察报告。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.logic.en: Both uses rest on the same thing: A is either the basis for judging B or the origin of a name or custom. It appears in expository writing, word origins and observation reports.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.connection.zh: 动词・い形容词普通形／な形容词词干＋な・である／名词＋である＋ことから
n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.connection.en: Verb or i-adjective plain form / na-adjective stem + な or である / noun + である + ことから

n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.contrast.zh: 它不是当事人辩解，所以别用在“我迟到了，因为……”这种场合。看到“有个特征→得出结论”或“有个特征→取了名字”，才是它。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.contrast.en: It is not a personal excuse, so do not use it for I was late because. It belongs where a feature leads to a conclusion, or a feature produces a name.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.translation.zh: 因为建筑形状像船，所以被称为“船之家”。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.4.translation.en: Because the building looks like a ship, it is called the Ship House.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.5.logic.zh: 极简洁、公式化，用一句话说清原因和处理结果。只出现在告示、公告、标牌、商务通知里，不用于日常解释。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.5.logic.en: Extremely compact and formulaic, giving cause and consequence in one line. It belongs to notices, signs and business announcements, never to everyday explanations.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.5.contrast.zh: 跟朋友解释个人理由不能用它，会像贴告示。看到「改装中」「工事中」「満席」这类公告语境，才读成“因……，故……”。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.5.contrast.en: It cannot explain a personal reason to a friend — it would sound like a posted notice. Only in contexts such as under renovation, roadworks or fully booked does it mean due to.

n2.day9-cause.grammar.5.translation.zh: 因店内正在装修，故今日暂停营业。
n2.day9-cause.grammar.5.translation.en: Closed today while the shop is being refitted.

n2.day9-cause.question.0.explanation.zh: 客观说明大雪导致高速公路封闭，「大雪のため」的接续和书面语气都合适。
n2.day9-cause.question.0.explanation.en: 大雪のため objectively explains that heavy snow caused the expressway closure. Its connection and written register fit the sentence.

n2.day9-cause.question.1.explanation.zh: 这是对比赛取消原因的客观说明，不是个人辩解。题干中逗号已给出，补「ため」。 补充：ことから可基于台风接近这一事实说明决定，だけに强调其影响，ものだから较口语地解释原因；ため更适合中性报告。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ため」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.1.explanation.en: Target expression: ため. Intended meaning: A neutral report of the cause, rather than a personal excuse. Compared alternatives: ことから / だけに / ものだから. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.1.anchor.en: A neutral report of the cause, rather than a personal excuse.

n2.day9-cause.question.2.explanation.zh: 说话人正在交代自己没说好的理由，带有解释和辩解感，用「ものだから」。 补充：ことから较书面；ばかりに带“就因为这点而吃亏”的后悔。ものだから在解释失误时自然，但不是唯一可接的原因形式。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ものだから」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.2.explanation.en: Target expression: ものだから. Intended meaning: A personal explanation or excuse. Compared alternatives: ことから / ばかりに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.3.explanation.zh: 向对方解释自己迟到的理由，比客观报告式的「ため」更符合这个场景。 补充：ために是中性原因，だけに可强调拥堵带来的后果；ものだから更有解释／辩解口气。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ものだから」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.3.explanation.en: Target expression: ものだから. Intended meaning: A personal explanation or excuse. Compared alternatives: ために / だけに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.4.explanation.zh: 就因为贪便宜立即买下，结果反而付出昂贵修理费，是「ばかりに」典型的后悔与坏结果。 补充：这些形式均可说明因果；ばかりに最直接突出“一时贪便宜导致吃亏”的懊悔。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ばかりに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.4.explanation.en: Target expression: ばかりに. Intended meaning: Regret about an action that led to an unfavorable outcome. Compared alternatives: ことから / ために / だけに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.4.anchor.en: Regret about an action that led to an unfavorable outcome.

n2.day9-cause.question.5.explanation.zh: 泄露秘密成了关系恶化的导火索，带有“早知道就不说”的遗憾。 补充：ものだから解释失言原因，ことから较书面说明因果；ばかりに更突出后悔。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ばかりに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.5.explanation.en: Target expression: ばかりに. Intended meaning: Regret about an action that led to an unfavorable outcome. Compared alternatives: ものだから / ことから. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.5.anchor.en: Regret about an action that led to an unfavorable outcome.

n2.day9-cause.question.6.explanation.zh: 正因为准备了很久，失败的冲击才更大，前项加强后项用「だけに」。 补充：ばかりに可后悔投入过多，ことから可客观说明震动大的原因；だけに强调投入越多越失落。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「だけに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.6.explanation.en: Target expression: だけに. Intended meaning: A reason that makes the emotional result stronger. Compared alternatives: ばかりに / ことから. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.6.anchor.en: A reason that makes the emotional result stronger.

n2.day9-cause.question.7.explanation.zh: 正因为是人气作家的新作，关注度才更高。这里是结果加强，不是公告中的原因。 补充：につき也可以郑重陈述原因，虽较像说明或公告；だけに更自然地强调名作家新作应有的关注度。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「だけに」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.7.explanation.en: Target expression: だけに. Intended meaning: A reason that increases the expected level of attention. Compared alternatives: につき. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.7.anchor.en: A reason that increases the expected level of attention.

n2.day9-cause.question.8.explanation.zh: 樱花树多是地名的由来，表示命名根据时用「ことから」。 补充：ために、ものだから、だけに也能表达树多与命名的因果；说明名称由来的书面表达常用ことから。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ことから」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.8.explanation.en: Target expression: ことから. Intended meaning: A written explanation of the origin of a name. Compared alternatives: ために / ものだから / だけに. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.8.anchor.en: A written explanation of the origin of a name.

n2.day9-cause.question.9.explanation.zh: 把窗户开着当成判断有人从此进入的线索，用「ことから」。 补充：ものだから也能以开窗这一事实解释自己的推断，较口语；ことから更清楚地把它当作证据。 本题按题面给定的意思和语气计分，只接受「ことから」。上述其他可成立的表达用于比较，不属于本题的目标答案。
n2.day9-cause.question.9.explanation.en: Target expression: ことから. Intended meaning: Evidence used as the basis for an inference. Compared alternatives: ものだから. Some alternatives can form grammatical sentences, but change the focus, strength or register. Scoring follows the nuance specified in the question.

n2.day9-cause.question.9.anchor.en: Evidence used as the basis for an inference.

n2.day9-cause.question.10.explanation.zh: 这是工事现场的正式告示，「工事中につき」表示“因施工，故不可使用”。
n2.day9-cause.question.10.explanation.en: This is a formal construction-site notice. 工事中につき means that the facility cannot be used because construction is in progress.

n2.day9-cause.question.11.explanation.zh: 店铺以公告口吻说明今日包场，名词后接「につき」最符合。
n2.day9-cause.question.11.explanation.en: The shop will give an announcement indicating that today’s wrapping is the most suitable place for "につき" after noun.

word.8.meaning.en: Mr.; Ms. (polite suffix after a name)

word.9.meaning.zh: 亲昵称呼后缀，常用于孩子或亲近的人
word.9.meaning.en: affectionate name suffix, often used for children or close friends

word.10.meaning.zh: 称呼后缀，常用于男性同辈或晚辈
word.10.meaning.en: name suffix used for juniors or peers, often male

word.12.meaning.en: teacher; doctor (also used as a title)

word.28.meaning.zh: 多大年纪（询问年龄的礼貌说法）

word.33.meaning.en: nice to meet you; I'm glad to make your acquaintance

word.34.meaning.en: Nice to meet you; I look forward to working with you.

minna.lesson.1.grammar.1.meaning.zh: 「は」先把话题点出来，「です」再给判断，一句话说清「A 是 B」。
minna.lesson.1.grammar.1.meaning.en: は sets the topic and です carries the judgement: one pattern for "A is B".

minna.lesson.1.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 把「です」换成「じゃありません」，同一句话立刻变成「A 不是 B」。
minna.lesson.1.grammar.2.meaning.en: Swap です for じゃありません and the same sentence turns into "A is not B".

minna.lesson.1.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 句尾加「か」，陈述句就变成问句，语气仍然客气。
minna.lesson.1.grammar.3.meaning.en: Add か at the end and a statement becomes a polite question.

minna.lesson.1.grammar.4.meaning.zh: 「も」顶替「は」，表示「也一样」，把前面刚提过的内容整块接过来。
minna.lesson.1.grammar.4.meaning.en: も replaces は to mean "too", inheriting whatever was just said.

minna.lesson.1.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 「の」把两个名词粘在一起，前一个说明后一个的归属、单位或类别。
minna.lesson.1.grammar.5.meaning.en: の glues two nouns together: the first qualifies the second.

minna.question.1-1.translation.zh: 礼貌地介绍自己的职业：我是银行职员。
minna.question.1-1.translation.en: Introduce yourself politely: I'm a banker.

minna.question.1-1.explanation.zh: 名词直接接です。ます接动词的ます形词干；这里不加を或の。
minna.question.1-1.explanation.en: A noun connects directly to です. ます attaches to a verb stem; neither を nor の is needed here.

minna.question.1-2.translation.zh: 澄清身份：我不是学生，是公司职员。
minna.question.1-2.translation.en: Clarifying identity: I am not a student, I'm an employee of the company.

minna.question.1-2.explanation.zh: 名词的礼貌否定用じゃありません／ではありません；くありません用于い形容词。
minna.question.1-2.explanation.en: Negate a noun with じゃありません or the more formal ではありません. ～くありません is used with i-adjectives, not nouns.

minna.question.1-3.prompt.instruction.zh: 初次见面，不知道对方是不是医生。选出询问身份的一句。
minna.question.1-3.prompt.instruction.en: On meeting someone for the first time, ask whether they are a doctor.

minna.question.1-3.translation.zh: 需要提问，而不是替对方作判断。
minna.question.1-3.translation.en: Questions need to be asked, not judged.

minna.question.1-3.explanation.zh: 礼貌问句在です后加か。「医者です」是陈述；否定和过去式都没有询问当前身份。
minna.question.1-3.explanation.en: ですか forms a polite question. 医者です is an affirmative statement; it is neither negative nor past tense.

minna.question.1-4.translation.zh: B也来自中国，要表达“我也是”。
minna.question.1-4.translation.en: B is also from China, to say “Me too”.

minna.question.1-4.explanation.zh: 前后国籍相同，用も表示“也”；の连接名词，を标记宾语，で不能在此表示“也”。
minna.question.1-4.explanation.en: The nationality is the same before and after, using も for "also" ; の connects noun, を tags for guests, and で cannot be used here for "also".

minna.question.1-5.translation.zh: 说明自己是樱花大学的学生。
minna.question.1-5.translation.en: She is a student of Sakura University.

minna.question.1-5.explanation.zh: 大学の学生用の连接所属单位与身份；大学に学生です不成立。
minna.question.1-5.explanation.en: 大学の学生 uses の to connect an institution and a role. 大学に学生です is not grammatical.

minna.question.1-6.translation.zh: 你不是学生，而是公司职员。选出前后一致的回答。
minna.question.1-6.translation.en: You're not a student, you're an employee of the company. Choose a consistent answer.

minna.question.1-6.explanation.zh: 先用いいえ否定“是学生”，再说明是公司职员。回答必须对应对方问的身份，不能把はい当成通用开场白。
minna.question.1-6.explanation.en: First use いいえ to deny being a student, then explain that you are a company employee. Answer the identity asked about; はい is not a general opening phrase.

word.486.meaning.en: boarding area; taxi stand; bus stop

word.502.meaning.zh: 实在不好意思；非常抱歉（也可用于感谢对方费心）
word.502.meaning.en: I am very sorry; thank you for going to the trouble.

word.507.meaning.zh: 虚构的超市名称（原表记待核对）

minna.lesson.10.grammar.1.meaning.zh: 存在句：某处有某物用「あります」，有人或动物用「います」。
minna.lesson.10.grammar.1.meaning.en: Existence: あります for things, います for people and animals.

minna.lesson.10.grammar.1.translation.en: There's a book on the table.

minna.lesson.10.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 主题句：已知的人或物在哪，用「は」提出、场所放后面。
minna.lesson.10.grammar.2.meaning.en: Topic sentence: a known thing or person, then where it is.

minna.lesson.10.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 方位词接在「の」后面，说明具体位置，后面通常再加「に」。
minna.lesson.10.grammar.3.meaning.en: Position words follow の and usually take に.

minna.lesson.10.grammar.3.translation.en: The bank's in front of the station.

minna.lesson.10.grammar.4.meaning.zh: 「や」举几个代表，暗示还有别的；「と」则是全部列清。
minna.lesson.10.grammar.4.meaning.en: や lists examples and implies more; と lists everything.

minna.lesson.10.grammar.4.translation.en: There are photographs, letters, etc. in the boxes.

minna.question.10-1.translation.zh: 描述院子里有一只活着的猫。
minna.question.10-1.translation.en: Describe a living cat in the yard.

minna.question.10-1.explanation.zh: 人和动物的存在一般用います；无生命物品用あります。
minna.question.10-1.explanation.en: The presence of humans and animals is generally used as います; there are no living objects as あります.

minna.question.10-2.translation.zh: 以老师为主题，说明老师的位置。
minna.question.10-2.translation.en: The subject is teachers, indicating their position.

minna.question.10-2.explanation.zh: 存在位置用に。教室で教えます才是动作发生的地点。
minna.question.10-2.explanation.en: Use に for the location of existence. 教室で教えます uses で for the location of an action.

minna.question.10-3.translation.en: The bank is used as a reference for the location.

minna.question.10-3.explanation.zh: 参照名词＋の＋方位名词：銀行の隣。后面的に标记存在地点。
minna.question.10-3.explanation.en: Reference noun + の + location noun: 銀行の隣. The following に marks the location of existence.

minna.question.10-4.translation.zh: 只列举一部分物品，还有其他东西。
minna.question.10-4.translation.en: Just a few items and something else.

minna.question.10-4.explanation.zh: や与など呼应，列举代表性的物品，而不是只限这两样。
minna.question.10-4.explanation.en: や echoes など by listing representative items rather than being limited to both.

minna.question.10-5.translation.en: It means there's a computer in the classroom.

minna.question.10-5.explanation.zh: 场所に＋物が＋あります，既要区别に／で，也要区别あります／います。
minna.question.10-5.explanation.en: Place に＋object が＋あります. Distinguish に from で and あります from います.

minna.question.10-6.translation.zh: 田中在会议室；回答位置，不是动作。
minna.question.10-6.translation.en: Tanaka is in the conference room; answer position, not action.

minna.question.10-6.explanation.zh: 人用います，存在地点用に，两项都要配对正确。
minna.question.10-6.explanation.en: People use います and there are places where に is available, both paired correctly.

word.508.meaning.en: to be absent; to take a day off

word.509.meaning.en: to take (a resource, e.g. time or money)

word.510.meaning.en: be in Japan; stay in Japan

word.527.meaning.en: counter for flat objects such as paper or stamps

word.544.meaning.zh: 哥哥（称呼哥哥或说别人的哥哥）

word.565.meaning.zh: 慢走；路上小心（送人出门时用）
word.565.meaning.en: have a good day; take care

word.566.meaning.zh: 慢走；路上小心（送人出门时用）
word.566.meaning.en: Take care; see you when you get back.

word.567.meaning.zh: 我出门了（行ってきます的郑重说法）

word.568.meaning.en: I'm off (and will be back later); see you later

minna.lesson.11.grammar.1.meaning.zh: 「三つ」「二枚」这类数量词不抢位置，插在助词后面、动词前面，句子照样顺。
minna.lesson.11.grammar.1.meaning.en: Counting words like 三つ and 二枚 slot in after the particle and before the verb.

minna.lesson.11.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 「二年」「三か月」说的是持续了多久，直接放在动词前，后面不带助词。
minna.lesson.11.grammar.2.meaning.en: 二年 and 三か月 say how long something lasted; they sit right before the verb with no particle.

minna.lesson.11.grammar.2.translation.en: Has studied Japanese for two years.

minna.lesson.11.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 一段时间里做几次，用「期間＋に＋回数」，这里的「に」不能省。
minna.lesson.11.grammar.3.meaning.en: How many times within a period: period + に + count. The に is not optional.

minna.lesson.11.grammar.4.meaning.zh: 问「要花多久」，用「から～まで どのくらいかかりますか」，问时间也问钱。
minna.lesson.11.grammar.4.meaning.en: Ask how long something takes with から～まで どのくらいかかりますか; it covers time and money alike.

minna.lesson.11.grammar.4.translation.en: How long from Tokyo to Osaka?

minna.lesson.11.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 「ぐらい」配数量，「ごろ」配时间点：一个管多少，一个管几点。
minna.lesson.11.grammar.5.meaning.en: ぐらい goes with amounts, ごろ with clock times: one counts how much, the other when.

minna.question.11-1.translation.zh: 买了四个苹果。数量词直接放在动词前。
minna.question.11-1.translation.en: Buys four apples. Quantum words are directly in front of verb.

minna.question.11-1.explanation.zh: りんごを四つ買いました中四つ直接修饰动作，不再加を或に。
minna.question.11-1.explanation.en: In りんごを四つ買いました, 四つ directly modifies the action. Do not add を or に to the counter.

minna.question.11-2.translation.zh: 表示昨天学习持续了三个小时。
minna.question.11-2.translation.en: It says that yesterday's study lasted three hours.

minna.question.11-2.explanation.zh: 持续长度用三時間，后面通常不加に。三時に是三点这个时刻。
minna.question.11-2.explanation.en: 三時間 expresses duration and normally takes no に. 三時に refers to the time three o'clock.

minna.question.11-3.translation.zh: 说明每个月看两次的频率。
minna.question.11-3.translation.en: Indicate the frequency twice a month.

minna.question.11-3.explanation.zh: 期间に＋次数表示单位期间内的频率，与持续时间不加に的句型不同。
minna.question.11-3.explanation.en: The number of に + times indicates the frequency of the unit period, which is different from the type of sentence that does not exist for the duration of に.

minna.question.11-4.translation.en: Ask for the time required to reach the station.

minna.question.11-4.explanation.zh: どのくらいかかりますか问需要多久；何時问钟点，不能与十分这个时长回答对应。
minna.question.11-4.explanation.en: どのくらいかかりますか asks how long it takes; when to ask the clock, it cannot correspond to a very long answer.

minna.question.11-5.translation.zh: 想表达“大约七点起床”，不是睡了七小时。
minna.question.11-5.translation.en: It's not like you've been sleeping for seven hours.

minna.question.11-5.explanation.zh: 时刻附近用ごろ：七時ごろ。表示大约时长则用七時間ぐらい。
minna.question.11-5.explanation.en: Use ごろ for an approximate time: 七時ごろ. For approximate duration, use 七時間ぐらい.

minna.question.11-6.explanation.zh: 七時間是持续长度，大约数量用ぐらい，不能用表示时点的ごろ。
minna.question.11-6.explanation.en: Seven hours is a continuous length, about a quantity of ぐらい, which cannot be used to indicate the time point ごろ.

word.583.meaning.en: light (i.e. not heavy); feeling light (i.e. offering little resistance, moving easily)

word.584.meaning.zh: 想选～；～比较好（如我选咖啡）

word.602.meaning.en: sashimi (raw sliced fish, shellfish or crustaceans)

word.604.meaning.zh: 天妇罗（裹面糊油炸的食物）
word.604.meaning.en: tempura; deep-fried fish and vegetables in a light batter

word.605.meaning.en: ikebana; Japanese art of flower arrangement

word.607.meaning.zh: 哪一个；哪边（比较两者时用）

minna.lesson.12.grammar.1.meaning.zh: 名词和な形容词的过去全靠句尾「でした」扛，否定是「じゃありませんでした」。
minna.lesson.12.grammar.1.meaning.en: For nouns and な-adjectives the past lives entirely in the ending: でした, negated as じゃありませんでした.

minna.lesson.12.grammar.2.meaning.zh: い形容词的过去是把词尾「い」换成「かった」，否定换成「くなかった」：变的是词本身，不是句尾。
minna.lesson.12.grammar.2.meaning.en: For い-adjectives the word itself changes: い becomes かった, negated as くなかった. The ending stays です.

minna.lesson.12.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 「より」标出比较的基准：谁在前面，谁就更胜一筹。
minna.lesson.12.grammar.3.meaning.en: より marks the yardstick. Whoever comes first wins the comparison.

minna.lesson.12.grammar.3.translation.en: The tram is faster than the bus.

minna.lesson.12.grammar.4.meaning.zh: 两个里挑一个，用「どちらが」；回答给「～のほうが」。
minna.lesson.12.grammar.4.meaning.en: Pick one of two with どちらが; answer with ～のほうが.

minna.lesson.12.grammar.4.translation.en: Which do dogs and cats prefer?

minna.lesson.12.grammar.5.meaning.zh: 三个以上比高低，范围用「の中で」，冠军用「いちばん」。
minna.lesson.12.grammar.5.meaning.en: Three or more: の中で sets the field, いちばん crowns the winner.

minna.lesson.12.grammar.5.translation.zh: 日本料理中最喜欢什么？
minna.lesson.12.grammar.5.translation.en: What's the favorite thing in Japanese food?

minna.question.12-1.translation.en: I've had time to say yesterday.

minna.question.12-1.explanation.zh: な形容词礼貌过去肯定用词干＋でした，不能像い形容词一样接かった。
minna.question.12-1.explanation.en: な adjective used to use words to dry + でした and cannot receive かった like い adjective.

minna.question.12-2.translation.zh: 楽しい的过去肯定，表示旅行很开心。
minna.question.12-2.translation.en: 楽しい must have been a good trip in the past.

minna.question.12-2.explanation.zh: 楽しい去い＋かったです。です已经负责礼貌，不再叠加でした。
minna.question.12-2.explanation.en: Replace the final い of 楽しい with かったです. です already makes it polite; do not add でした.

minna.question.12-3.translation.zh: 以巴士为基准，说新干线更快。
minna.question.12-3.translation.en: The bus was used as a benchmark, saying that the new trunk line was faster.

minna.question.12-3.explanation.zh: 比较基准用より；N1はN2より～表示N1比N2更……。
minna.question.12-3.explanation.en: Compare the base with より; N1 は N2 より ~ means N1 is more than N2.

minna.question.12-4.translation.zh: 回答两者中更喜欢冬天。
minna.question.12-4.translation.en: The answer to both is that winter is preferred.

minna.question.12-4.explanation.zh: 二者比较的回答用冬のほうが好きです；より放在比较基准后，不能说よりが。
minna.question.12-4.explanation.en: For a comparison of two items, answer 冬のほうが好きです. より follows the comparison standard; よりが is not grammatical here.

minna.question.12-5.translation.zh: 在水果这个范围中问最喜欢什么。
minna.question.12-5.translation.en: Ask what's the favorite in the fruit range.

minna.question.12-5.explanation.zh: 先用の中で限定范围，再用いちばん询问最高程度。
minna.question.12-5.explanation.en: Use の中で to specify the group, then いちばん to ask for the highest degree.

minna.question.12-6.translation.zh: 難しい的过去否定：考试不太难。
minna.question.12-6.translation.en: 難しい has been denied in the past: it's not so hard to get an exam.

minna.question.12-6.explanation.zh: い形过去否定是去い＋くなかったです。难度不高需要否定，不能选肯定过去。
minna.question.12-6.explanation.en: い has been denied in the form of い + くなかったです

minna.question.12-7.translation.zh: 名词休み的礼貌过去否定：上周一不是休息日。
minna.question.12-7.translation.en: Noun 休み's courtesy used to deny: last Monday was not a day off.

minna.question.12-7.explanation.zh: 休み在这里是名词，过去否定用じゃありませんでした；休みませんでした是动词休む的过去否定。
minna.question.12-7.explanation.en: 休み here is noun, which used to deny the use of じゃありませんでした; 休みませんでした is the previous rejection of verb 休む.

minna.question.12-8.translation.zh: 把いい变成过去肯定，表示天气很好。
minna.question.12-8.translation.en: Change いい to the affirmative past form to say that the weather was good.

minna.question.12-8.explanation.zh: いい的过去形式使用よい的词干，变成よかったです。
minna.question.12-8.explanation.en: The previous version of いい uses the header of よい to become よかったです.

word.618.meaning.en: to play (games, sports); to enjoy oneself

word.620.meaning.en: to go out to meet; to receive

word.624.meaning.zh: 出去；离开（如离开咖啡馆）

word.654.meaning.en: What would you like to order?

minna.lesson.13.grammar.1.meaning.zh: 想要东西用「N が ほしいです」，助词是「が」，不是「を」。
minna.lesson.13.grammar.1.meaning.en: Wanting a thing: N が ほしいです. The particle is が, not を.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 想做某事，把「ます」换成「たい」：变的是动词本身，不是往后面加词。
minna.lesson.13.grammar.2.meaning.en: To want to do something, swap ます for たい. The verb changes; nothing is tacked on the end.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.2.note.zh: 先还原ます形并去ます：食べます→食べ→食べたい；行きます→行きたい。たい按い形容词变化：行きたくない・行きたかった。描述第三人的愿望常用「～たがっています」或转述「～たいと言っています」。
minna.lesson.13.grammar.2.note.en: Remove ます from the masu-form: 食べます→食べ→食べたい; 行きます→行きたい. たい conjugates like an i-adjective: 行きたくない・行きたかった. For another person's desire, use ～たがっています or report it with ～たいと言っています.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.2.translation.en: I want to go to Kyoto.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 去某地「为了」做某事：目的地用「へ」，目的用「动词ます＋に」。
minna.lesson.13.grammar.3.meaning.en: Going somewhere to do something: へ marks the destination, Vます＋に marks the purpose.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.3.translation.en: Go pick up a friend at the station.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.4.meaning.zh: 疑问词加「か」，就把「哪里」变成「某个地方」：不确定，但确实存在。
minna.lesson.13.grammar.4.meaning.en: Question word plus か turns "where" into "somewhere": unsure, but real.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.4.note.zh: 何か（を）食べます＝吃点什么；どこかへ／に行きます＝去某处。不能把所有助词都任意省略。疑问词＋も与否定连用时如「何も食べません」，意思是“什么也不吃”。
minna.lesson.13.grammar.4.note.en: 何か（を）食べます means eat something; どこかへ／に行きます means go somewhere. Not every particle can be freely omitted. A question word + も with a negative, as in 何も食べません, means not eating anything.

minna.lesson.13.grammar.4.translation.zh: 休假时去了什么地方吗？
minna.lesson.13.grammar.4.translation.en: Did you go somewhere on vacation?

minna.question.13-1.translation.zh: 表达自己想要一台新相机。
minna.question.13-1.translation.en: Say you want a new camera.

minna.question.13-1.explanation.zh: ほしい表达想要物品，欲望对象用が。想做动作则用动词词干＋たい。
minna.question.13-1.explanation.en: ほしい expresses a desire object using が. If you want to do something, verb is used to dry + たい.

minna.question.13-2.translation.zh: 行きます→“我想去北海道”。题干后已有です。
minna.question.13-2.translation.en: 行きます: "I want to go to Hokkaido." There are now です.

minna.question.13-2.explanation.zh: 行きます去ます得到行き，再加たい。不是辞书形行く直接接たい。
minna.question.13-2.explanation.en: Remove ます from 行きます to get 行き, then add たい. Do not attach たい directly to the dictionary form 行く.

minna.question.13-3.translation.zh: 用迎えます表达去车站接朋友。
minna.question.13-3.translation.en: Use 迎えます to describe going to the station to meet a friend.

minna.question.13-3.explanation.zh: 移动目的接ます形词干＋に行きます：迎えます→迎えに行きます。
minna.question.13-3.explanation.en: For the purpose of movement, use the masu-stem + に行きます: 迎えます→迎えに行きます.

minna.question.13-4.translation.zh: 还没决定吃什么，想吃点东西。
minna.question.13-4.translation.en: I haven't decided what to eat yet. I want something to eat.

minna.question.13-4.explanation.zh: 何か是不确定的某物；何も通常与否定呼应，だれか指人。
minna.question.13-4.explanation.en: 何か refers to something unspecified; 何も normally pairs with a negative. だれか refers to a person.

minna.question.13-5.translation.zh: 行きたい的否定：今天不想出门。
minna.question.13-5.translation.en: Negative of 行きたい: do not want to go out today.

minna.question.13-5.explanation.zh: たい按い形容词变化，去い＋くない，得到行きたくないです。
minna.question.13-5.explanation.en: たい conjugates like an i-adjective. Replace final い with くない: 行きたくないです.

minna.question.13-6.translation.zh: 明确购物是去百货公司的目的。
minna.question.13-6.translation.en: Makes it clear that shopping is the purpose of the department store.

minna.question.13-6.explanation.zh: 活动名词可以直接接に行きます：買い物に行きます，不需要の。
minna.question.13-6.explanation.en: An activity noun can directly precede に行きます: 買い物に行きます. No の is needed.

word.659.meaning.en: to turn off (a light, TV, heater, etc.); to switch off

word.660.meaning.en: to open (a door, etc.); to unwrap (e.g. parcel, package)

word.666.meaning.en: to hold (in one's hand); to take

word.674.meaning.en: to fall (of rain, snow, ash, etc.); to come down

word.679.meaning.en: address (of a home, business, etc.); residence

word.684.meaning.zh: ～的方法（ます形去ます后接方）

word.689.meaning.en: a bit more; a bit longer

word.692.meaning.zh: 来吧；开始吧（催促或鼓励）

word.696.meaning.zh: 请用这个（付款时：用这张钱结账）
word.696.meaning.en: I would like to pay with this.

minna.lesson.14.grammar.1.meaning.zh: 请对方做某事，动词换成て形再接「ください」。
minna.lesson.14.grammar.1.meaning.en: Ask someone to do something: て-form plus ください.

minna.lesson.14.grammar.2.meaning.zh: 正在做某事，用「て形＋います」，就是中文的「正在」。
minna.lesson.14.grammar.2.meaning.en: て-form plus います is the plain "is doing" of Chinese 正在.

minna.lesson.14.grammar.3.meaning.zh: 主动揽活：「我来帮你……吧？」用「ましょうか」。
minna.lesson.14.grammar.3.meaning.en: Offer a hand: ましょうか means "shall I do that for you?"

minna.lesson.14.grammar.3.translation.en: Can I help you with your luggage?

minna.lesson.14.grammar.4.meaning.zh: て形不是背出来的，是按词尾分组换出来的：先认组，再换尾。
minna.lesson.14.grammar.4.meaning.en: The て-form is not memorised one verb at a time. Identify the group, then swap the tail.

minna.lesson.14.grammar.4.note.zh: 先确定动词组别。五段：う・つ・る→って（買って・待って・帰って）；む・ぶ・ぬ→んで（読んで・遊んで・死んで）；く→いて（書いて）；ぐ→いで（泳いで）；す→して（話して）。特例：行く→行って。一段：去る＋て（食べて・見て）。三组：する→して、来る→来て（きて）。「帰る・入る」等是五段，不能只凭る结尾判断。
minna.lesson.14.grammar.4.note.en: Identify the verb group first. Godan: う・つ・る → って (買って・待って・帰って); む・ぶ・ぬ → んで (読んで・遊んで・死んで); く → いて (書いて); ぐ → いで (泳いで); す → して (話して). Exception: 行く → 行って. Ichidan: remove る and add て (食べて・見て). Irregular: する → して; 来る → 来て (きて). 帰る and 入る are godan verbs: an ending in る alone does not identify the group.

minna.question.14-1.translation.zh: 待ちます：请在这里稍等。
minna.question.14-1.translation.en: 待ちます: Please wait here.

minna.question.14-1.explanation.zh: 请求用て形＋ください。待つ是五段つ结尾，て形是待って。
