chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.0.zh: 累了的时候、寂寞的时候、压力积攒的时候，很多人会听音乐让心情放松。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.0.en: Many people listen to music to relax when they are tired, lonely, or stressed.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.1.zh: 我们听到喜欢的音乐，心就会平静下来，也会忘掉寂寞。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.1.en: When we hear music we like, our mind calms down and we forget our loneliness.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.2.zh: 另外，听到自然中的声音，比如海浪声、小鸟的叫声，心也会被治愈。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.2.en: Sounds in nature, such as waves or birdsong, can also heal the heart.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.3.zh: 像这样利用音乐和声音来消除压力、让身体恢复活力，就叫做“音乐疗法”。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.3.en: Using music and sound this way to relieve stress and restore the body is called “music therapy.”

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.4.zh: “音乐疗法”的方法多种多样：听音乐、唱歌、跟着歌做手部游戏、演奏乐器等。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.4.en: Music therapy takes many forms: listening, singing, hand games to songs, playing instruments.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.5.zh: 最简单的方法大概就是“听”吧。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.5.en: The simplest method is probably listening.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.6.zh: 那么，听什么样的音乐才好呢？
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.6.en: So what kind of music should one listen to?

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.7.zh: 听讨厌的音乐，当然不可能放松。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.7.en: There is no way you can relax while listening to music you dislike.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.8.zh: 只有听自己喜欢的音乐，才是真正的心灵疗愈。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.8.en: Listening to music you love is what truly heals the heart.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.9.zh: 因此，喜欢古典乐的人听古典乐、喜欢演歌的人听演歌，才是有效的方法。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.9.en: So the effective way is for classical fans to listen to classical music and enka fans to enka.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.10.zh: 另外，也有这样的例子：难以用语言交流的人，和音乐治疗师一起唱歌、演奏，渐渐就能与人交流了。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.10.en: There are also cases where people who struggled to communicate in words gradually opened up by singing and playing with a music therapist.

chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.11.zh: 音乐和声音会给压力重重的现代社会带来怎样的效果，今后大概会更受关注。
chukyu.lesson.1.reading.0.example.11.en: What effect music and sound have on our stressful modern society will draw more attention from now on.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.0.zh: 在你们国家，人们认为什么样的数字是“好数字”，相反什么样的数字是“坏数字”？
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.0.en: In your country, which numbers are considered “good” and which “bad”?

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.2.zh: 在越南，人们认为“4”这个数字是好数字之一。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.2.en: In Vietnam, 4 is considered one of the good numbers.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.3.zh: 偶数是“有伙伴”的，所以是好数字。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.3.en: Even numbers are good because they have a partner.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.4.zh: 但在日本和汉语圈，“4”因为和“死”同音而被嫌弃。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.4.en: In Japan and Chinese-speaking regions, however, 4 is disliked because it sounds like “death.”

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.5.zh: 不同的国家，吉利数字和不吉利数字是不一样的。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.5.en: Lucky and unlucky numbers differ from country to country.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.6.zh: 不过，好像没有哪里像汉语圈这样讲究“好数字”。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.6.en: Yet nowhere seems as particular about good numbers as Chinese-speaking regions.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.7.zh: 就用车牌号码为例来介绍吧。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.7.en: Let me use license plates as an example.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.8.zh: 在香港，念起来意思吉利的“18（必定发财）”非常受欢迎。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.8.en: In Hong Kong, “18” (certain to get rich) is hugely popular because it sounds auspicious.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.9.zh: 因此，这个号码曾在拍卖会上拍出数千万日元以上令人吃惊的价格。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.9.en: That number once fetched a startling price of tens of millions of yen at auction.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.10.zh: 在日本，只要抽签抽中，热门号码（如1或8888）只付手续费就能拿到，所以对日本人来说简直难以想象。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.10.en: In Japan you can get a popular number (1 or 8888) for just a fee if you win the lottery, which is unimaginable to Japanese.

chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.11.zh: 在香港，似乎有人比起开什么车，更看重挂什么号码的车牌。
chukyu.lesson.2.reading.0.example.11.en: In Hong Kong, some people seem to care more about the plate number than about the car itself.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.0.zh: 来日本以后，“面白い（有意思）”这个词我已经听过很多次了。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.0.en: Since coming to Japan, I have heard the word omoshiroi many times.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.1.zh: 也常被人说“玛丽亚·埃莱娜，你很有意思啊”。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.1.en: People often told me, “Maria Elena, you're interesting.”

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.2.zh: 这是在夸我呢，还是在取笑我呢？
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.2.en: Was that praise, or was I being teased?

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.3.zh: 我渐渐明白的是：“面白い”是带有好意的词，并不是否定性的。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.3.en: What I came to understand is that omoshiroi is a favorable word, not a negative one.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.4.zh: 日本很有意思。日本人也有意思。住在日本这件事也有意思。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.4.en: Japan is interesting. Japanese people are interesting. Living in Japan is interesting too.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.5.zh: 不用说，还有一本正经的日本。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.5.en: Needless to say, there is also earnest Japan.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.6.zh: 通勤电车里充满了这种气氛。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.6.en: The commuter train is full of that atmosphere.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.7.zh: 可是，深夜的电车满是酒气——爱喝酒的日本。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.7.en: But the late-night train reeks of alcohol: drinking Japan.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.8.zh: 虽说物价高，可各种东西都免费发放——便宜的日本。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.8.en: Prices are said to be high, yet many things are given away free: cheap Japan.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.9.zh: “地面易滑请注意”“请勿忘带物品”“请注意正在关闭的门”。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.9.en: “Watch your step, the floor is slippery.” “Don't forget your belongings.” “Mind the closing doors.”

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.11.zh: 可是重复太多，啰嗦的日本。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.11.en: But with so much repetition: noisy Japan.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.12.zh: 工作时非常亲切的日本人。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.12.en: At work, Japanese people are very kind.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.13.zh: 但一走出职场，人就变了。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.13.en: But once out of the office, they change.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.14.zh: 在电车上推开别人抢座位的失礼的日本人。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.14.en: The rude Japanese who shoves others aside to grab a seat.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.15.zh: 我想，住在国外，无论在哪个国家都会有有趣的发现。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.15.en: I think that living abroad brings interesting discoveries in any country.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.16.zh: 尤其我是从地球的另一端来的，文化和习惯不同并不奇怪。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.16.en: In my case especially, coming from the other side of the globe, differences in culture and custom are no wonder.

chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.17.zh: 在日本生活了大约十年，已经习惯了这里的生活，但每天仍有意想不到的事情发生，我依然觉得日本很有意思。
chukyu.lesson.3.reading.0.example.17.en: After about ten years in Japan I am used to life here, yet something unexpected happens every day, and Japan still strikes me as interesting.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.0.zh: 阳光照进眼睛时，或者从昏暗的室内走到明亮处、刚觉得刺眼的一瞬间，有时会打出喷嚏。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.0.en: Sometimes a sneeze bursts out the moment sunlight hits your eyes or you step from a dark room into brightness and feel dazzled.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.1.en: This is called the photic sneeze reflex.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.2.zh: 本来，喷嚏是想把进入鼻子的异物连同鼻涕一起推出去而发生的反射运动。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.2.en: A sneeze is originally a reflex that tries to push foreign matter out of the nose along with mucus.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.3.zh: 灰尘等进入鼻子、吸入冷空气等都会成为诱因。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.3.en: It is triggered by dust entering the nose or by breathing in cold air.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.4.zh: 可是，接收光的是眼睛而不是鼻子，为什么会打喷嚏呢？
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.4.en: But it is the eyes, not the nose, that take in light, so why does a sneeze happen?

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.5.zh: 这是因为眼睛发出的“刺眼”信号在传向大脑的途中，不知为何刺激了引起喷嚏的神经，于是鼻子发痒，打出喷嚏。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.5.en: The “too bright” signal from the eyes, on its way to the brain, somehow stimulates the nerve that triggers sneezing, so the nose tingles and a sneeze comes out.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.6.zh: 与花粉症这类过敏不同，“光喷嚏反射”的喷嚏只打一次，最多两三次。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.6.en: Unlike allergies such as hay fever, a photic sneeze comes once, or at most two or three times.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.7.zh: 据国内外调查，据说有两三成的人有“光喷嚏”的自觉症状。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.7.en: Surveys in Japan and abroad say that twenty to thirty percent of people notice this photic sneeze symptom.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.8.zh: 而且人们认为这种症状会遗传给子孙。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.8.en: The trait is also thought to be inherited by one's descendants.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.9.zh: 话说回来，日语里表示喷嚏的声音一般是“はくしょん（哈啾）”，实际的声音又如何呢？
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.9.en: By the way, Japanese usually writes a sneeze as hakushon, but what does it actually sound like?

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.10.zh: “へくしゅ”“はっくしょい”“くしゅん”等等，因人而异。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.10.en: It varies from person to person: hekushu, hakkushoi, kushun, and so on.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.11.zh: 有趣的是，还有说法称喷嚏声亲子之间一模一样，打喷嚏的方式也有男女差异。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.11.en: Interestingly, some say parents and children sneeze alike, and that men and women sneeze differently.

chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.12.zh: 喷嚏是很有意思的生理现象。
chukyu.lesson.4.reading.0.example.12.en: A sneeze is a fascinating physiological phenomenon.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.0.zh: 过了九月中旬，早晚凉了一些，变得好过多了。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.0.en: Past the middle of September the mornings and evenings have cooled a little, and it has become easier to live.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.1.zh: 我住的公寓附近有个叫三井公园的公园。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.1.en: Near the apartment where I live there is a park called Mii Park.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.2.zh: 从公寓走着绕公园一圈再回来，大约45分钟。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.2.en: Walking from the apartment around the park and back takes about forty-five minutes.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.3.zh: 正好是合适的散步路线，所以休息日的早晨我常去。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.3.en: It is just the right walking course, so I often go on holiday mornings.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.4.zh: 那座三井公园也渐渐显出秋意了。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.4.en: That park, too, is beginning to show signs of autumn.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.5.zh: 我来介绍一下这个公园。

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.6.zh: 第一张照片是从公园入口拍的。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.6.en: The first photo was taken from the park entrance.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.7.zh: 这个公园禁止自行车穿行，所以入口处设了挡自行车的栏杆。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.7.en: Bicycles may not pass through the park, so barriers are set up at the entrance.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.8.zh: 公园是围绕一大一小两个池塘建造的。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.8.en: The park is built around two ponds, one large and one small.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.9.zh: 这张照片是较小的那个池塘。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.9.en: This photo shows the smaller pond.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.10.zh: 这个小池比大池更接近自然，透着宁静的景致。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.10.en: This pond is closer to nature than the large one and has a quiet air about it.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.11.zh: 沿池边的小路走一点就有长椅。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.11.en: A little way along the path by the pond there is a bench.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.12.zh: 满是落叶，总觉得很有秋天的样子吧。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.12.en: It is covered with fallen leaves, a scene that somehow feels like autumn.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.13.zh: 常看到有人坐在这张长椅上，一边晒着秋日的阳光一边读书。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.13.en: I often see people sitting on this bench reading in the autumn sun.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.14.zh: 最后一张照片是孩子们开心玩耍的样子。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.14.en: The last photo shows children playing happily.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.15.zh: 来公园歇口气的人很多，所以这里笼罩着平和的气氛。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.15.en: Many people come here to take a breather, so the park is wrapped in a gentle mood.

chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.16.zh: 住处附近有这样的公园，是一件幸福的事。
chukyu.lesson.5.reading.0.example.16.en: It is a happy thing to have a park like this near where you live.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.0.zh: 在日本，一年四季都能买到烤鳗鱼。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.0.en: In Japan you can buy grilled eel all year round.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.1.zh: 然而在“土用丑日”（7月20日前后），其销售额会飙升到年平均的二十几倍。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.1.en: But on the day of the ox in midsummer (around July 20) sales jump to more than twenty times the yearly average.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.2.zh: 对许多人来说，土用丑日大概就是“不吃鳗鱼就过不下去的日子”。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.2.en: For many people the day of the ox is “the day you cannot help eating eel.”

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.3.zh: 土用丑日吃鳗鱼的习惯，似乎源自江户时代“防苦夏吃鳗鱼好”这句广告语。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.3.en: The custom of eating eel on that day seems to have come from an Edo-period advertising line: “Eel is good for preventing summer fatigue.”

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.4.zh: 如果真是这样，那这句广告的效果已经持续了两百多年。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.4.en: If true, that ad has kept working for more than two hundred years.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.5.zh: 短期内销量集中的商品，除鳗鱼之外还有“情人节巧克力”“圣诞蛋糕”等，而近来逐渐固定下来的是“节分的粗卷寿司”。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.5.en: Other products with sales concentrated in a short period include Valentine's chocolate and Christmas cake, and the newest to take hold is the thick rolled sushi of Setsubun.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.6.zh: 这原本是关西“吃惠方卷”的习惯。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.6.en: This was originally a Kansai custom of eating ehomaki.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.7.zh: 据说“节分那天朝着惠方［吉利的方向］，一口气吃完粗卷寿司，那一年就会有好运”。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.7.en: It is said that if you face the auspicious direction on Setsubun and eat a whole thick roll in one go, good luck will come that year.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.8.zh: 大型便利店连锁把这个关西的习惯带到了关东并推广开来。
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.8.en: A major convenience store chain brought this Kansai custom to the Kanto region and spread it.

chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.9.zh: 由商业主义催生的新饮食习俗，会像“土用丑日的鳗鱼”那样，两百年后依然留存吗？
chukyu.lesson.6.reading.0.example.9.en: Will eating habits born of commercialism, like eel on the day of the ox, still be around two hundred years from now?

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.0.zh: 任何职业都有辛苦的一面和有趣的一面。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.0.en: Every profession has its hard side and its interesting side.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.1.zh: 相扑界在具有这种两面性这一点上也一样。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.1.en: The world of sumo wrestlers shares that same two-sidedness.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.2.zh: 首先要进入“部屋”这个组织。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.2.en: First you join an organization called a heya, a stable.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.3.zh: 入门后的一段时间里，从早到晚都和同一部屋的人在同一个地方吃住。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.3.en: For a while after joining you live and eat day and night in the same place as everyone in your stable.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.4.zh: 分给新弟子的活儿很多。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.4.en: New disciples are given a lot of work.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.5.zh: 每天早上四点半起床，不吃早饭就进行晨练。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.5.en: They get up at 4:30 every morning and train without breakfast.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.6.zh: 冬天再冷也是光着身子赤着脚。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.6.en: Even in cold winter they are bare-chested and barefoot.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.7.zh: 弄得满身沙子、满是伤痕地拼命练。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.7.en: They train hard until they are covered in sand and bruises.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.9.zh: 之后在浴室给师兄们搓背。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.9.en: After that they wash their seniors' backs in the bath.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.10.en: They are the very last to bathe.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.11.en: Those on cooking duty prepare the meals.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.12.zh: 收拾完餐具等之后，趁师兄们午睡时打扫和洗衣服。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.12.en: After clearing the dishes they clean and do laundry while the others nap.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.13.zh: 做完之后，到傍晚可以午睡，因为不好好休息身体就长不胖。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.13.en: Then they nap until evening, because without rest the body cannot put on weight.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.14.en: Those on duty must cook dinner too.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.15.zh: 再收拾一遍，才终于能睡下。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.15.en: They clear up again and finally go to sleep.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.16.zh: 每天早上到来，都重复同样的事。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.16.en: Each morning the same routine repeats.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.17.en: The amount they eat is astonishing.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.18.zh: 放大量肉类、鱼贝类、豆腐、蔬菜等、被称为“相扑火锅”的菜，要吃很多。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.18.en: They eat plenty of chanko nabe, a dish packed with meat, seafood, tofu, and vegetables.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.19.zh: 此外，体重轻的新人力士被要求睡前至少吃两碗茶泡饭和十根香蕉。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.19.en: On top of that, lighter new wrestlers are told to eat at least two bowls of rice with tea and ten bananas before bed.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.20.zh: 新人力士中也有边哭边吃的。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.20.en: Some new wrestlers eat while crying.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.21.zh: 但是，变强之后，相扑就变得有趣了。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.21.en: But as they get stronger, sumo becomes interesting.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.22.zh: 因为有趣，就更加刻苦练习。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.22.en: Because it is interesting, they train even harder.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.23.zh: 于是更能赢了，赢了排名就会上升。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.23.en: Then they win more, and winning raises their ranking.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.24.zh: 排名上升，工资也涨，赢了还能拿奖金，努力就清清楚楚地变成了看得见的成果。
chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.24.en: A higher rank means better pay and prize money for wins, so the effort takes clear, visible shape.

chukyu.lesson.7.reading.0.example.25.en: That is why it is interesting.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.0.zh: 人的第一印象是由什么决定的呢？
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.0.en: What decides a person's first impression?

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.1.zh: 决定人的印象的要素可分为语言性的和非语言性的。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.1.en: The factors that shape an impression divide into verbal and nonverbal ones.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.2.zh: 语言性要素指话语和说话内容，非语言性要素指视觉信息（来自眼睛的信息）和听觉信息（来自耳朵的信息）。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.2.en: Verbal factors are the words and content of speech; nonverbal factors are visual information (from the eyes) and auditory information (from the ears).

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.3.zh: 视觉信息指服装、肢体语言等，听觉信息指声调、说话方式。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.3.en: Visual information means clothing and body language; auditory information means tone of voice and manner of speaking.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.4.zh: 有说法称，仅凭语言性要素判断对方的人只有百分之几。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.4.en: One theory says only a few percent of people judge others by verbal factors alone.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.5.zh: 也有人极端地说“人的印象百分之百靠外表”。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.5.en: Some even say, extremely, that “looks are one hundred percent of an impression.”

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.6.zh: 那么，我们来想想非语言性要素吧。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.6.en: So let us consider the nonverbal factors.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.8.zh: 这并不是只要注意服装就行，表情、姿势、动作也是重要的一点。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.8.en: It is not enough to mind your clothes; expression, posture, and movement matter too.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.9.zh: 例如，露出笑容、与对方对视，能传达对对方的信任。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.9.en: Smiling and meeting the other person's eyes, for example, convey trust.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.10.zh: 相反，面无表情就让人感觉不到干劲。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.10.en: A blank face, on the other hand, gives no sense of motivation.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.11.zh: 另外，前倾的姿势看起来像是没有自信。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.11.en: A hunched posture also looks lacking in confidence.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.12.zh: 过度靠在椅背上，可能给人压迫感。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.12.en: Leaning too far back in a chair can come across as intimidating.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.14.zh: 说话时，要注意让声调、音量和速度与场合相称。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.14.en: When speaking, take care that your tone, volume, and speed suit the situation.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.15.zh: 虽说一般都讲“人重要的是内在”，但外表和说话方式会极大左右人的第一印象，这似乎是事实。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.15.en: It is commonly said that what matters is the inside, yet looks and speech clearly sway first impressions a great deal.

chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.16.zh: 因此，为了更有效地传达自己想说的内容，也有必要注意自己的外表和说话方式。
chukyu.lesson.8.reading.0.example.16.en: So to get your message across more effectively, you also need to mind your appearance and the way you speak.
